reviews.review:
We came in a group of 4 and the dishes are on the smaller side. We got drinks (all delicious - my favorite was the beets n cream), 3 small plates, 4 mains, and one side and it left me feeling satiated without being too full.

Small Plates
- Uni and crab tartlet (5/5): this bite was so delicious, fresh, and creamy from the uni. My favorite bite of the night for sure

- Yum Khai Dao (4/5): this salad was so fun! The flavors were vibrant and the trout roe added a nice texture

- Yum Som O (4.5/5): -0.5 points since this dish was TINY, but it was such a refreshing appetizer with fresh, citrus flavors. I loved it!

Mains
- Pork Jowl (4.5/5): loved the crispy rice. pork jowl was good, but not the best pork jowl I ever had! It was a nice, savory dish though with the perfect crispy texture

- Ba Jang Lobster (5/5): my favorite main. the lobster was so juicy and soft and I loved the sticky rice! 

- Chilean Sea Bass Curry (4/5): My least favorite main. I think I was not a huge fan of the spice of this dish, but others in my group loved it!

- Beef Cheeks Curry (4.5/5): Preferred this curry since it was not spicy! The beef was also so tender and it tasted so good with the rice

- Green Beans (4.5/5): Nothing special, but was necessary!

The dishes were also paced well and brought out quickly! Might be my new favorite thai restaurant in the city :)

I was seated with a friend for its Kitchen View in the rear of the restaurant, and was very impressed with the lighting, service, and quality of our meal. Bangkok Supper Club is a cozy West Village spot with bar, traditional seating, and kitchen-side seats that go quick!

The food is served family-style, with many dishes easily shareable between small and large parties. Our server recommended one small plate and one large plate per person, but we both felt one entree and side was plenty. The portion sizes are excellent. We ordered the Pork Jowl, which was highly recommended, and the meat was extremely tender and the rice was flavorful. Our green beans and snow pea side dish also made a great balance with the meat.

For starters, we chose the fried wings that were stuffed with sticky rice. They were easy to share, and you can also request an extra (i.e., each order comes with three) if you prefer equal portions. The octopus was also delicious, and the fried onions and sauce was the highlight of the dish.

Our dessert was also a pleasant surprise! Kudos to the service for clearing our plates and utensils, recommending fan favorite dishes (that also became the top dishes for us too), and also providing coat check and storage in the front of the restaurant. The bill will run a bit more expensive, but I firmly believe it's worth every dollar for the high-quality food and experience you'll receive.

this was literally one of the best meals that I had with my friends when we came to New York! We made the reservation for the 4 of us 3 weeks in advance. When we got in, we were able to coat check and be seated immediately. 

We ordered a bunch of dishes off the menu to share and honestly, I don't think I can pick my favorite one because they were literally all that delicious ! The service was amazing all night and they were super attentive to any of our needs. It's pretty dimly lit inside, but I guess that gives it a high class feel.

Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche (4.5/5): This dish was super interesting to me because of the watermelon which lent a sweet taste to the scallops. It worked really well together, and I would totally get it again. 

Goi (5/5): A little bit spicier than I expected, but I love a spicy dish so that worked out perfectly. This is basically beef tartare with Thai spices. 

Pork Jowl (5/5): I was literally speechless when I had a bite of this because I wasn't expecting it to be so flavorful. The rice on the bottom was deliciously garlic, and the pork gel on top was crispy and every bite was a masterpiece.

Bangkok Gai Yang (5/5): Another one of the hits of the night. This was a marinated yummy chicken dish. It came with a spicy sauce on the side that elevated it to a different level. My friends and I also use the sauce on the pork jowl!

Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry (4/5): This was a great dish. Disclaimer: I'm just not the biggest fan of curry. I will say that the beef was extremely tender, so that was lovely.

Pandan Cake Dessert (4.9/5): This was honestly probably one of the best pandan desserts I have ever had in my life. I am not really sure what this is called because we kind of just asked for the coconut dessert that everyone seemed to be getting. The cake was layered with a delicious cream frosting, and the coconut still had some meat inside for us to pick up.

Fish Sauce (3/5): I was unfortunately, a little bit, disappointed by this drink and probably would not get it again because it did not feel like there was good flavor. Not a bad drink overall-- just underwhelming

I had a great time here!
I came with 2 other friends and decided to share 3 entrees and a side. We were pleasantly stuffed by the end!
All the dishes were super flavorful and well presented. My friends liked the sea bass cur du the most and I surprisinglyreallly liked the chicken with sticky rice and snowpeas. We all agreed the pork jowl was a bit too salty and dry but nevertheless we enjoyed everything!

After many sleepless nights of looking up a reservation on Resy, which opens up every midnight for 30 days in advance, Finally got lucky and glad my efforts were not ir vain.

I might write tons of adjectives praising this but to sum it up - "OUTSTANDING"

The food was some of the best I've had this year, Starting from the Uni Crab Tartlets, to the charred Bok Choi, to the Grilled Prawn Satay, to the Ba Jang Lobster and finally ending with the Coconut Pandan Dessert. Each dish was perfection like I've never seen before. The falvor depth in each bite was truly something spectacular.

We did order some of their in-house specialty drinks, Truffled Pandan and the Fish Sauce, they were unique but might not be for everyone's liking !

As you would expect from a place like this the service was fantastic.

Reserve this one for your special days and you won't be disappointed.
Best Thai restaurant I've been to. So worth the price. If you can get a reservation here DO IT. Everything from the appetizers to dessert was literal perfection.

Went here for post Valentine's Day date night. Everything about this place was perfect - the ambience, service and the food. The food perfectly showcased the Chef's creative take on authentic Thai flavors. Tried the Prawn Satay, Beef Tartare, Pork Jowl and Green Beans - can't pick the best because all of them were amazing. Special shoutout to the ice cream which was a pandan cake served in a coconut.
Since we didn't have a reservation, we got a counter seat at the Kitchen which gave us a front seat to the chefs mastery. The head chef was super nice and even a took a picture of us.

My partner and I are avid fans of Thai food, having been to some of the most exciting Thai restaurants in Bangkok, southern Thailand, and across the U.S., and we were especially eager to try Bangkok Supper Club when it first opened to see whether it might be able to match the great Thai fine dining restaurants of California (Nari, Kin Khao, etc.).

While our first few times here were enjoyable, it's become apparent that Bangkok Supper Club is increasingly resting solely on its Instagram laurels, celebrity appeal, and prime location with little interest or commitment to hospitality or pushing the boundaries of fine Thai cuisine. Despite being open for nearly two years, Bangkok Supper Club maintains essentially the same large course menu as when it opened, with many of the dishes leaving much to be desired. The Massaman beef cheek curry is a blatant copycat of a dish from Michelin-starred Kin Khao but lacking in aromatic complexity and flavor; the chakram sea bass curry is similar in profile to gang kua but timid and whitewashed in its spice profile and stingy on the portion of fish; the lobster is a confused, breathless dish rightfully called out by the New York Times as an expensive Instagram thirst trap; and the pork jowl desperately needs nam jim jaew as an accompaniment to balance its excessive fattiness and chewiness.

Equally as disappointing as the increasingly beleaguered main course menu has been the declining standards of hospitality at BSC - apparently the staff here are sure enough of their social media status such that service is no longer required. In our most recent visit - a birthday no less - we were seated at an extremely small table despite being longstanding, repeat customers who clearly labeled this as a birthday event in the reservation and ordered 7 dishes (as an aside: no birthday freebies or accompaniments here!). Because of this, the restaurant was not able to serve our main dishes together as they should have been. Most frustrating of all, the first-time couple next to us who ordered less than half of the amount of food was seated at a large table. Service was inconsistent and at times inattentive, and we ultimately had to flag our server down to grab the (large) bill after waiting around for more than 15 min.

My spouse and I had been regular customers here, but we will not be returning until BSC figures out how to refocus on cuisine and service. Perhaps start by remembering who we are next time after all of the business we've given you?

We were celebrating my birthday. The food was overall decent, particularly the small plates. However, the large plate selection continues to disappoint--largely unchanged since they opened, mundane, and not hearty enough. 

What especially annoyed us was the fact that it was my birthday, yet we were given a small table. We were clearly there to spend (come on, have a better business sense), but there wasn't enough space for the seven dishes we ordered. Ironically, a couple next to us was seated at a large table for four, seemingly there just for an Instagram moment, barely ordering any food.

We were early fans and regulars at one point, but these recurring misses in both food and service have let us down significantly. The restaurant also lacks a system for recognizing and valuing its regular customers who actually spend on the food. I believe this place and its chef have the potential to break through to the next level, but they seem stalled by their fixation on perfecting the Instagrammable vibe over prioritizing food and service.

I made reservations on the Thursday for Saturday, and limited to 4 or 9 PM reservation due to its popularity. I chose the 4 PM slot for two people and when we arrived on Saturday, the host promptly led us to our table. At the entrance, they offered coat check for our winter jackets. 

Our server Mont was very knowledgeable and he took the time to explain the drinks menu in detail as we were excited to try several drinks but couldn't pick one. We ended up ordering the Fish Sauce and Butterfly Pea Tea. I was pleasantly surprised by how well the flavors blended in with each other - I would have never expected a combination of Napa cabbage broth and fish sauce to be a components of an alcoholic beverage. The square ice cube in the drink was branded with "Bangkok Supper Club" which added a nice touch. The Butterfly Pea Tea was exactly what we expected to get and a solid drink for a cold day. 

Mont suggested that we consider two small bites, two small plates, and two large plates. We ordered two Uni and Crab Tartlets, a Grilled Mushroom Salad, the Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche, Pork Jowl, Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry, and String Beans. I loved the Uni and Crab Tartlet since it's not a common menu item at restaurants. Since the cost of uni and crab are expensive, the small bite was on the pricier side at $22 a piece. I really enjoyed the Grilled Mushroom Salad - the salad had the right amount of sauce so I didn't feel like I was eating greens alone or too much sauce to drown the leaves. The Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche fell short of expectations and I would probably pass on it if I were to revisit this restaurant. Both the Pork Jowl and Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry were delicious, but I think the Pork Jowl with fried rice score higher on my list than the curry. If I were given a choice between a curry dish from Bangkok Supper Club or Fish Cheeks, their sister restaurant, I would choose the latter. My only complaint about the meal were the String Beans. About a third of the beans were too charred for our liking so we ended up discarding them which feels like a waste of $16. There were two dessert options: sweet potato ice cream and pandan cake. We chose the Pandan option and it came in a coconut with coconut crème on top and toasted coconut flakes. The Pandan cake was moist and fluffy, and there were also pieces of coconut meat that we scraped off the side of the coconut. I was quite impressed by the dessert. 

The restaurant was quiet when we first arrived at 4 PM and quickly became more lively as the night progressed. The candle on the table was a nice touch as the restaurant was dimly lit. There are some larger tables that are booth-style for parties of 6. I enjoyed where we sat as it was along the wall and away from other tables giving a spacious feel.

Loved everything about this place. 
Vibes were chill but clean and chic. 
They literally won an award for their cocktails and they're definitely creative and different. We tried 4 different drinks and everything was great and they have a broad range of flavor profiles and strengths. 
For apps we got a few things. The rice stuffed chicken wings which had great flavor and were easy to eat. The Hokkaido scallop ceviche was very refreshing but more of a summer dish. The watermelon and mint overwhelmed the scallops but still light and refreshing, definitely not the favorite of the night. We were going to order both the toro tartare, which was the special for the night, and the steak tartare but our waiter said they had a similar flavor profile so we got the toro tartare. This was our favorite app for sure. Very light and refreshing with different textures coming from the lettuce, the fried onions and the fish itself. It was pretty spicy so be warned. 
For entrees we got the pork jowl which was essentially a fancy pork fried rice and we got the crying tiger. The pork jowl dish was delicious. Again had varying flavors and textures. The crying tiger was the steak and it was cooked perfectly and had a delicious sauce on top. 
The service was great and everyone was very attentive. 
Overall, this was a great place for a date night but definitely on the pricier side so maybe save this for a special occasion. I'd come back!

Heard a lot about this, impossible to get reservations and thank God for my friends for getting one. Got a booth for 4, comfortable, near the bar, the place is nice but not overtop with the decor which made me think the food must be good. We took a glance and realized it was easier naming what we didn't want to order. We ordered the whole menu besides the sides of vegetables, no steak, no eggplant, no mushroom salad, and didn't get the small bites. From the appetizers or smaller plates, wings are an absolute must, egg salad, grape fruit, scallops, and octopus were also very good. Skip the prawns, the beef tartare, and the beef tongue. Nothing special. For the mains the lobster is underwhelming, nothing special at all. Everything else was good, but the seabass curry wasn't anything special. A little too spicy for my taste. Loved both desserts. Oh for drinks, I'm sober but I got the mango cocktail as a mocktail and it was good. The table got the strawberry, and the guava cocktails. They said they liked them. Overall would definitely come back.
Absolutely amazing. Excellent food. Couldn't get enough. Very nice ambiance. Great bartender. Very nice people here. I'm going back for the char grilled chicken. It was to die for.

This was an incredible dining experience!!! Everything we had to eat was excellent and we shared multiple apps and dishes amongst the party of four I dined with. The cocktails were phenomenal as well. One of my more enjoyable dining experiences I've had in Manhattan while visiting.

We visited for the second time last week with a group of six. The food was as excellent as the first time - we ordered the mushroom salad, scallop ceviche, beef cheeks massaman, Gai Yang, and Sea Bass and a couple others. We had both desserts, which were the stars of the meal. The food and drinks were incredible. The only downside was how rushed the meal felt. We ordered at least ten plates, which were all delivered in two batches. We had to ask the server for recommendations rather than them helping to guide us. I think for the price, I was disappointed by the service overall. There wasn't much care (ad maybe time) to make sure we were able to enjoy the meal properly. There are so many diverse tastes and flavors. I still have to give this place five stars, though. The food is impressive from start to finish. We would return for sure.

Service was good, especially the coat check and attentive staff, but food was lacking as we had expected stronger flavors and overall better tasting options. We came for the ambiance and drinks, but primarily enjoyed the booths as drinks were OK.

reviews.review: Sat at the bar at Bangkok supper club and liked the Hokkaido scallop ceviche (spicy watermelon scallop ice appetizer). We also had the beef cheeks massaman curry and pork jowl rice. The coconut pandan dessert was really good and the presentation was wonderful too. It's like cake with coconut jelly with cream on top.

I was torn between 4 and 5 stars for this one. The food was really good but not worth the hard to get reservations. You can get same quality Thai food from Thai diner or Thai villa but there were some standouts. The scallop is so worth it! The uni wasn't worth the price. Drinks were phenomenal! I would go back and try a few more things but I'll wait for the hype to die down a little
The food was delicious, the service was amazing. I enjoyed every bite and can't wait to go back.

"Not the Bangkok I know"

Came here with a 6 top to try this place which has good reviews on Eater. But having tried it, I have mixed feelings about this place. While trying to go upscale + fusion I think they lose some essence of great Thai food. Also wasn't impressed with the service.

What's to cheer
- Some really tasty and unique dishes: Pork Jowl, Lobster (though small), Beef Tongue and Green Beans. Lots of flavors in these, presented well and good portion sizes.
- Pandan cocktail with truffle is great.

What's to jeer
- Decor isn't unique or cool or anything but meh
- Drinks vary quite a bit and one was completely way too sour and not balanced. They wouldn't remake it and made my friend pick something else! 12 years in the liquor industry and that's a first for me. It tasted off
- Grilled bok choy: 6 pieces for $18? And nothing special?
- Branzino, Mushroom salad, Sea Bass and Prawns, and both desserts were ok, but not memorable.
- Service could me more friendly and engaging, especially at this price point. Save the 'tude, it's 2025!

I've been to BSC twice now, and the food is consistently good. The scallop and beef tartare appetizers were exactly what I remembered from my visit last year - both are standout dishes, along with the pork jowl main. Our server was very enthusiastic about recommending the chicken thigh, which I found to be the least impressive dish here. Tasty enough, but the only BSC item I've tried that I think a competent cook could easily recreate at home.

The prices are pretty steep for what you get, even by NYC standards. BSC doesn't post menu prices on their website, which is probably my single biggest restaurant pet peeve. Unlike printing menus, it doesn't cost the restaurant anything whatsoever to update prices on an online menu. Sus behavior if you ask me. People go to a restaurant's website for a few pieces of information that should always be there: hours & location, menu WITH PRICES, and reservation/contact info. That's it. All else is fluff.

Upon entering the restaurant, I was greeted by two hosts. They were very professional and took our coats. The restaurant was warm and inviting. They have a many luxurious sea green booths, which were very cozy. 

The menu has plenty of options. 
--Pork jowl - very expertly fried and the rice underneath was heaven. 
--Scallop ceviche - unexpectedly had a very spicy kick.
--The string beans were cooked well and al dente. 
--Gai yang chicken was extremely soft and well marinated. Definitely get this!
--Chicken wing stuffed with sticky rice had interesting contrasting flavors and textures
--Beef tongue was something fun to try. The texture was new to me, but I enjoyed it.
--Pandan dessert in a coconut shell, delicious
--Sweet potato ice cream was very unique and I liked this better than the coconut 

For better or worse, I took my toddler here. She loved the bangkok gai yang, and string beans. There was not much else she could eat because of her toddler-ness. 

The plates are quite pricey. For 4 adults (and 1 tot), the total with tax and tip was around $400. I was about 80% full. The food is very good quality. It is rare nowadays to get good quality food, even if it is quite expensive. However, Bangkok supper club delivers!  I would come back!

I went here with 3 other friends and we all had the same takeaway WOW! We ordered family style and were not disappointed with anything. For me, the highlight was the Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry.

The restaurant was definitely on the pricey side but well worth it. I would definitely come back here for a special occassion!

I wish I could give half stars, as I've had a mixed experience coming here.

The Good:
- Unique cocktails containing a variety of interesting components such as clarified milk
- Approachable and tasty appetizers
- Chic/moody ambiance, setting a tone for a fun night out with friends or a date 

The Bad:
- The acoustics here make it terribly difficult to hear others (and your server) when it's crowded. Great if you're looking for a bustling atmosphere, but not so good if you find this kind of environment overwhelming.
- I'd say pricey, but it's on par for what a "hip" spot in the area would cost
- Service was a little disappointing for our group as it seemed a little cold and awkward - unfortunately the 20% gratuity is mandatory for groups of 6 or more with no ability to adjust it reflective of the service received.

I wouldn't mind coming back but it's also not a place I'm itching to revisit.
The service was good and staff was very attentive. It is a beautiful restaurant. After having the dinner, I got a stomach bug so unfortunately I will not be returning.

I was here with a group of five others at this fancy Thai restaurant rather recently. The prices online aren't listed which has always irked me but in general the appetizers are in the low to mid $20s and the main dishes outside of the veggie ones are in the upper $30s to mid $40s outside of the $95 steak. (Thanks to other Yelpers for the menu photos.) I had dishes that other people on here recommended and I had a very tasty albeit very expensive meal. The space was nice and while I've heard it's loud, it wasn't really though perhaps this was because we were all the way in front and not by the tables in back, but I can't imagine it being super loud back there either. Shoutouts in particular goes to our female server who was very knowledgeable about both the dishes (such as allergens for some people as well as recommendations) as well as the cocktails and the like.

As they recently had won a Michelin award for their cocktail menu and as the drinks were interesting, I for once got two. The first one was the Smokey Milk for $21 with sake, Bombay Sapphire gin, pear cordial, fermented lychee fruit, and clarified milk which as the name suggests was smoked at the table. While I appreciated the presentation, the smoke was overpowering both in terms of odor as well as flavor and I had to let the drink sit on my tongue in order to be able to taste it. It was subtly sweet and refreshing with a light taste of ferment likely both from the sake and lychee but some of these flavors were presumably overpowered by the smoke which should be done but maybe half the time. The other drink was the Charred Pina for $23 with Mitcher's rye, artichoke liqueur, charred pineapple, and bergamot which was better. It had a slight bite from the rye and a subtle bitter fruity sweetness from the pineapple as well as the liqueur which I presume is Cynar. Other people had the Dirty Pineapple which they liked but found a bit boozy, someone had (several glasses of) wine, and someone had the mocktail version of the Beets 'n' Cream which they thought was unique but a bit too similar to a smoothie.

My appetizer was the Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche for $25 with Hokkaido scallop, pickled watermelon rind, diced watermelon, mint, and garlic topped with chili watermelon granita. As I like very spicy food and I love scallops, this was an easy choice. The granita was surprisingly spicy (even for my taste buds) and I wouldn't be surprised if it was bird's eye chili which contrasted with the plentiful plump sweet scallops. This was very tasty and very much worth it at the price point and I would recommend heavily for other folks who can handle chili.

A bunch of people had the Octopus for $22 listed as Bangkok-Chinatown style of deep fried octopus served with fried onions, sea beans, and pickled garlic sauce which they loved and seemed like a decent portion of octopus. Another person had the small bite Foie Gras Duck Breast Wrap ($19) which they thought was delicious and the last person who got an appetizer had the Grilled Mushroom Salad $21) which was notably larger than the other dishes and surprisingly came with a knife (they didn't say much.)

My main dish along with a bunch of others was the Pork Jowl for $36 with deep fried pork cheeks served with savory garlic baked rice topped with spiced pork cracklings. This was delicious but very rich. The pork cheeks were perfectly cooked with a light chew, as expected for jowl, while the baked rice was honestly better than the garlic rice at most Filipino spots with huge garlic flavor and a bit of charred texture. The little bits of pork cracklings were fatty and delicious but overall the dish was very rich and I think it needed more citrus outside of the lime that was provided. To accompany it, I would recommend the restaurant add either the nam jim jaew served with the Gai Yang or alternatively some type of chili sauce or chili dip/nam phrik which would both would work wonders in reducing the richness.

Another person loved the Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry ($43) and someone else loved the Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry ($38) and it seemed someone liked the Ba Jang Lobster ($38) but I didn't hear any comments from them (same person again.) 

This was a very expensive meal (and especially for Southeast Asian food) but at least for the dishes I had, it was excellent and at least mostly worth the price point. One cocktail had a bit too much smoke and I think the jowl needs something else along with the lime to cut the richness, but overall it was worth it. 4.5/bare 5

We got a last minute reservation through our Amex concierge and BOYYY we're  SO GLAD! BY FAR an amazing experience of different flavors on our palate.

The food is absolutely phenomenal. We started with the yum khai Dao (duck egg salad)--an exquisite balance of flavors, with an explosion of umami and spice that left our taste buds dancing. The pork Jowl was another highlight--perfectly cooked, with a crispy skin and tender meat, that was to die for. The  Curry was rich, fragrant, and spicy, with the perfect amount of heat and a coconut creaminess that felt like comfort in a bowl.

The drinks menu is equally impressive, featuring a mix of inventive cocktails and classic Thai-inspired drinks. I highly recommend the  pomegranate spritz--refreshing with just the right amount of depth.

Save room for dessert their coconut cake was refreshing and light and the perfect way to end our meal. 

Service was top-notch--our waiter was friendly, knowledgeable, and quick to offer recommendations. The pacing of the meal was just right, and we never felt rushed.

We will be back, by far the best meal we had during our time in NYC :)!

Chic cozy dim spotlighting interiors. Very nice. Service is great.
Below are the items I got and for 2 people it was a good order. I was full without room for dessert though.
Pork Jowl comes sliced in a bed of seasoned rice that is topped with crispies. Have you met these crispies? These crispies should be bagged and sold to snack on. I know polish delis sell the lard with these bits that you can fry in order to get these crispies. The dish itself is good. I enjoyed it and I also added some of the branzino sauce to oomph up the rice. The rice isn't spicy and since the apps were in the spicier side, I personally needed that oomph. 
Branzino - is beautiful and comes w a side lime fish sauce situation. It's for the most part deboned. We ordered a side of Crispy sticky rice that is 5" diameter. 
Stuffed chicken wings app- this was an unexpected delight! It's beboned and stuffed with lemongrassy sticky rice, get this - it's really fun and yummy.
Scallop ceviche granita - the scallops are silky delicious bright and light, the savory bright granita w a fish sauce lime punch and the small watermelon cubes all works really well. Get this!
Deep fried egg salad - this is visually a fun dish. There are two deep fried whole eggs that aren't flat, they are in the oval shape w some giant parsley leaves. Giant. This is a fun dish, tangy and for me spicy. 
Drinks- I got the beets n crème which was absolutely delicious. I love sweet desertty like drinks. This was like ice cream, I looooooooooved it

Visited last night, food was good but got seriously food poisoned (confirmed with a friend who has the same condition after dining here yesterday). Have been suffering from continuous nausea and vomiting since the visit. Stay away from this place if you don't want to be bedridden the next day :(

What an incredible dining experience. The spread was absolutely beautiful, and everything was fresh and so flavorful. The dining space is also elegant though it was a bit of a squeeze. Our waiter helped explain the various dishes in detail. I highly recommend trying the pork jowl and Chilean sea bass (the curry is SO good) -- both must-tries! I had the non-alcoholic mango flame which paired perfectly with the meal. We ordered the foie gras duck breast wrap which was fine but I'll probably skip it on future visits. Overall, it was such a lovely meal and dining experience. Will definitely be back.

Great upscale Thai spot, very trendy interior, dined twice and would return again. 

Would recommend asking the waiter for cocktail recommendations. There's several very unique cocktails. Truffled Pandan and Pak Chee were both like nothing I've had before.

Enjoyed pretty much everything I've eaten there, but noted the favorites.

Small Plates
- Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche (5/5) - This is the one to get. Generous amount of scallops under pile of watermelon ice.
- Octopus (4/5)
- Prawn Satay (4/5)
- Grilled Mushroom Salad (4/5)

Large Plates - Get the sea bass curry and pork jowl, just do it.
- Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry (5/5) 
- Pork Jowl (5/5) 
- Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry (4/5)

Fantastic experience here - my friend and I have been wanting to try it out but could never get reservations; we showed up at 4:55 for their 5pm opening time and luckily got seated right away. The food and drinks were not only delicious but also beautifully presented. Our waitress was also very knowledgeable about all the food/drinks and gave great recommendations; I enjoyed everything. You should definitely get the coconut pandan dessert - highlight of my meal! The price is definitely on the higher end, but I think it's worth it for the experience!

Loved the whole meal here! 

Favorites:

Grilled Mushroom Salad
Charred little gem lettuce, king oyster, oyster mushrooms, chrysanthemum shoots and Thai basil, sprinkled with coconut chips, served with coconut cilantro dressing.

Bangkok Gai Yang
Charcoal grilled chicken thighs marinated with lemongrass and cilantro, served with Nam Jim Jaew sauce with a side of charred sticky rice patty.

Green Beans
Charcoal grilled green beans, sweet peas, english peas, crispy garlic chili oil, tofu cream and crispy shallots

My friend says it's hard to make a reservation because they're always booked quickly! Luckily we get 
To snag one on a saturday. It's our first time here and it didn't disappoint! Cocktails are terrific! I had the beets and cream and its so yummy. Had the uni crab tartlet and foie gras small bites to begin and oh boy the taste is explosion! Had me excited for our meals. Ambiance is definitely aesthetic and clean. Even the bathroom is classy. Even the small amount of the mains got us satisfied and happy.

Stopped in here with a friend who has been here before, so he took care of the ordering, and we tried a lot!

First, get a reservation; it's crowded, the seats are small (my friend is tall and barely fit in the booth, but he loves it and said the food was worth it). Service was quick and efficient, changing out plates, watching the table to take empty dishes and bringing out food in good order. The concierge at the front was very quick to send us to seats, and we were started in very quick order... had a glimpse at their order system by the kitchen, very modern and efficient, I like it.

Thai in its original form is great - here, they were aiming to do new things with the different dishes and mix it up with a bunch of fusion dishes. Drinks up first, no iced tea, but they did have a lovely dried longan fruit drink that I enjoyed, not too sweet.

Small bites: Excellent start with these - they really set the tone. Take these as a single bite
* Uni & Crab Tartlet was excellent; grab with cocnut relish, in a tart form with Hokkaido uni and Ossetra caviar... rich, delicious, wonderful flavors and definitely worth it as a single large bite.
* Foie Gras Duck Breast Wrap was rich, grilled duck breast with foie gras, wrapped in a betel leaf, stuffed with mieng kham (also called miang, I think?) and cashews. Very delicious, very rich, wrap the leaf around and take it whole...

Small Plates: Good, but not outstanding for me...
-Prawn Satay (comes w/2, they brought out 3 for each of us at the table) - grilled tiger prawns with a little salad and currey cashew butter sauce, not bad, and at least properly cleaned prawns, cooked just right not to be tough and chewy.
- Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche - I'm torn, I like the idea of ice and fire (spicy) - pickled watermelon rind, diced watermelon, mint, garlic, topped with chili watermelon granite (frozen and spicy) - it was a strange, icy experience, with a bit too much fire for me (tone it back a bit and it'd be better balanced); scallop itself was beautiful, melt-in-your-mouth pieces (quartered?)
- Octopus was great - Bangkok-Chinatown style deep fried octopus with onions, sean beans and pickled garlic sauce. I liked the crispy and while a little oily, was well-cooked.

Large plates: Solid selections - all around very good:
* Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry was excellent with the fish, a touch of the curry sauce was enough for flavor. The white rice with a bunch of curry, less enjoyable. I had a bit of smoky metallic flavor to it, not bitter, but not quite my taste, but literally when we looked at the kitchen order system, every table ordered this but one... clearly a favorite here.
* Bangkok Gai Yang was excellent, chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, cilantro, and soy-based sauce with a little charred sticky rice patty (that was just ok)
* Crying Tiger was a delicious, super well-marbled 32 oz bone-in ribeye grilled, with a herb salad and tomato mash & garlic chips. The ribeye was cooked perfectly, but was a little sinewy in a couple pieces.
* Pork Jowl was deep fried and probably the weakest of all the large dishes, but was still fatty and rich, more pork cracklings would have been good here.

Sides: These were better than the small or large plates here... 
* Green Bean a little charcoaled like the Szechuan style, with garlic chili oil, shallots and tofu cream and with some peas
* Bok Choy was grilled, w/an anchovy oyster sauce, and fried anchovy crumbs. Big pieces, so would have been good if I had something other than a spoon to break it apart - knife?

Dessert: Two items not on the website, but they recommended and both were very good: 
* first an ice cream coconut with a cake underneath that was chewy and delicious- I have no idea what they called it, but it was beautiful in texture and just the right amount of ice cream to enjoy it with; I don't normally like coconut in focus, but this was excellent.
* a coconut pandan dessert filled with a whipped coconut creme, and below was a coconut jelly and cendol dessert mix.

Excellent food in the dessert, sides, and small bites. While the small plates didn't have the same bit of creativity or interest, the large plates made it mostly up. It tries a bit of creativity and flexibility and mostly succeeds. Nice pick, Corey!  James would be proud.

Trendy for a reason. Wow. Such an excellent meal. Everything was amazing, but highlighting my favorites. The massaman curry was unbelievable - massaman is not my go-to dish but the complexity and deepness of the flavors in this one was amazing. And the green beans, I could go on for hours. Perfectly charred with an excellent coconut sauce, a must order. Finally, the dessert here was phenomenal and so unique, we got both desserts and could not choose our favorite. 

Outside of the food, atmosphere is great. We were seated near the kitchen and had so much fun watching the dishes being plated. I would love to come back and sit at the chefs table. Great evening!

Thai is my favorite type of cuisine, and while I enjoy authentic neighborhood places, it had been quite a while since I had found a higher-end Thai establishment.  I fondly remember frequenting the swanky Kittichai in the early 2000's, but I cannot recall a similar type of restaurant since.  However, Bangkok Supper Club fit that bill precisely.  The sleek, modern dining room and elevated prices definitely took the place into a higher caliber. 

My friend and I grabbed seats at the bar and ordered cocktails.  I wound up loving the A-Jard Martini and ordered two rounds of the crisp, refreshing drink composed of Tepozan Tequila Blanco, sake, cucumber a-jard, and a dash of pandan.  The beverage packed a lot of cucumber flavor and, though it had a tequila base, I found it to very much resemble its namesake martini.  My companion ordered two different cocktails that she similarly enjoyed.  

While the small plates sounded good, we decided to share two main dishes instead, and they were both phenomenal!  The moist, tender Chilean Sea Bass was wild-caught and clearly of excellent quality.  It was served in a rich, spicy Chakram Curry broth.  The Beef Cheeks Massaman Curry similarly contained a delicately prepared protein in a creamy sauce, though this one was a bit thicker and less spicy.  Both main dishes were accompanied by sides of Jasmine rice.  If I had to choose, I would vote for the Beef Cheek Curry over the fish one, though my friend felt the opposite.  Funny enough, she is typically more of a meat eater than I am!

After the main portion of the meal, we decided to share the seductive Coconut Pandan dessert that we kept seeing delivered to other tables.  There was a coconut shell stuffed with a pandan cake, a pandan custard, and a coconut cream topping. There was also a side of toasted coconut flakes that we were told to sprinkle on the top to add some crunch.  I had not been very familiar with pandan at the time, but found the taste of the tropical plant similar to pistachio.  The dessert was heavenly and a must-order!

Our friendly and welcoming bartender/server delivered our check, which more expensive than I had expected (over $200), but I thought it was worth it for the delicious food, creative cocktails, and overall terrific meal.

The food here is amazing. I walked in with a group of 3 around 9 PM on a Saturday evening and was seated relatively quickly. We ordered a wide variety of dishes and drinks, largely at the recommendation of our very helpful server. 

DRINKS
Truffled Pandan - incredibly unique and adventurous. The truffle oil-clarified gin adds a hint of savoriness and truffle aroma, and the botanicals play nicely with the pandan. The coffee-infused apple juice and lactic acid add some gentle sweetness and tartness. All the elements are in perfect balance. 

Beets 'n' cream - sweet and subtly earthy, with a pleasantly creamy texture.

Mango flame - not bad, but pretty standard. Mezcal and some fruit notes. 

FOOD
Mushroom salad - great herb flavor from the cilantro, nutty notes from toasted coconut, savory and smoky flavor from the mushrooms, all tossed in a bright dressing. A really nice start to the meal. 

Grilled eggplant - the eggplant itself had a pleasant texture - still firm, but cooked through. The toppings form a nice flavor base with a great blend of flavors. 

Green beans - the green beans and sugar snap peas had just the right snap to them texturally, and the tart creamy base adds a nice flavor. Made for a good accompaniment to the eggplant.

My friends tried the gai yang and crying tiger. They loved the chicken, but thought the steak was just ok.

Overall, I found the meal to be very creative and well-executed. The total bill came out to about $365, so that puts this firmly in the fine dining category. Totally lives up to the hype.

food was phenomenal!!! our favorites were the pork jowl (crispy garlic rice was to die for), and the scallop ceviche (incredibly flavorful sauce/ice). the pandan dessert was also suuper good. sea bass curry was just ok. would love to be back!

This has been one of the highlight restaurants of the year for me. Incredible flavors that pop.

The chicken dish comes with a sauce that accents the dish incredibly well with a spicy and tangy kick

The green bean dish is a stand out and one of my favorite veggie sides I've had at a restaurant in recent memory. 

And the sea bass is served in a flavorful curry sauce.

Those three dishes are highlights. 

I've been twice now and the service is pretty strong as well.

Well worth the visit

Really great service overall, an aspect which impressed me the most! 

- There's a coat/bag check which is refreshing for a NYC restaurant (or maybe I need to start going to more high-end restaurants more!)
This came in clutch because my friends and I all came from work so we had our large backpacks, so the staff offered to check them in for us to avoid having them creep into the aisle.
- The server was helpful in letting us know how many dishes to order and saying optimize by splitting family style. Although we ordered under his recommendation - which turned out to be just the right amount of food btw - I appreciated his concern! When we put in our order for 2 small plates and 4 large plates, he was like "are you guys not that hungry?" lol. 
Reason for this is bc honestly more of the large plates appealed to us than the small plates, but we aren't made out of money like that to order a ton of large plates.
- When asking if we're ready to clear a plate and asked about dessert, the server didn't interrupt our conversation like some places I've dined at. They politely waited if we were mid-conversation to ask their question. This is really appreciated because so many times some NYC restaurants rush you to the point where they're just interrupting and ruining your dinner, so these small details really do matter.
- After small plates, staff cleared our plates AND silverware and replaced before our next course!

For the food...

Small Plates 
The small plate salads were good as starters - we ordered the Yum Khai Dao and Grilled mushroom salad. Some of the mushrooms pieces were a little tough/chewy but not in a bad way. We enjoyed the Yum Thai Dao slightly more, but it really was the large plates that took the center stage tonight. 

Large Plates 
We ordered the Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry, Grilled eggplant, and Bangkok Gai Yang (chicken), and Pork Jowl. 

My favorites: Pork Jowl and Bangkok Gai Yang.

Pork Jowl -  Loved the texture, and loved the crispiness of the pork and the crisps inside the fried rice!!

Bangkok Gai Yang - Loved how the chicken was cooked. Very tender meat but also had a crisp layer, and the sauce to dip was really yum. Personally didn't need even need the charred rice, which is what it's meant to be eaten with. The chicken alone was amazing and carried the flavor.

Sea Bass Curry - This fish curry was a tad bit on the sour side. | Pause: I googled Chakram curry, which is the type of curry it is, and Google noted it as "a spicy, hot, and slightly briny dish...that's made with dried red chilies and Makrut lime peels". So that makes sense, the brininess and hint of lime peel is what I may have been tasting. Unpause. |
I'm used to (and enjoy more) the sweeter curries, and that's a personal thing. For a small piece of fish with only one small bowl of rice to share amongst 4 of us (making it difficult to completely soak up the rest of the curry once everyone finished the fish), it's a bit difficult to say I would pay the $43 again for that dish.

The grilled eggplant was good; it was grilled eggplant. A good balance of texture and taste to the protein dishes though!

B/c of the food I was teetering between 4-5 stars, but given the ambiance and service themselves, I'll give a 5!

Nice ambiance that can be fit for a date night or evening out. Dim-ish lighting but there was a bright light above our table that didn't affect ambience but at least let us see our dishes very clearly, which is so nice and refreshing (Have you ever been in a dimly lit restaurant and you can barely see your food?!) VERY roomy seating: for a party of 4 we got one of the booths and it felt so nice to have elbow room in a NYC restaurant.

Overall yummy food and great dining experience to catch up with friends where we all left with satisfied bellies!

Food: Came here with a few of my friends! Ordered a few dishes and the best part of coming in a large group is that we can order several dishes and try a little bit of everything! Ordered several popular dishes along with some that looked very interesting however in the end, I wasn't too blown away as I would have expected based on the raving reviews that initially enticed me. 
We ordered: hokkaido scallop ceviche, lin yang, yum khai dao, grilled octopus, pork jowl, bangkok gai yang, whole branzino. The dishes were not really what I expected after all the hype I have heard from this place- I thought the popular pork jowl dish was okay. My favorite dishes were the hokkaido scallop ceviche and the dark meat of the bangkok gai yang. I also found the drinks to be average as well.

Cost: Average/above average pricing for a nyc dish

Environment: Super cuter interior! Loved the color and styling- it definitely added to the whole dining experience!
 
Service: The service that night was slightly on the slower side but I did notice that it was a full house and so I wasn't surprised!

Uniqueness: Delicious modern thai dishes!
Came here for dinner on a week night. Food was really good. The cocktails were ok. I don't really like the one with caviar. Our waiter was very attentive. Looking forward to my next visit!

Fantastic from start to end. We set at the chef's table so got a view a ton of dishes going out and they all looked amazing. The scallop ceviche dish was unique and very tasty. Crispy rice dish was fantastic. And to top it off, the cocktails were inventive and balanced.

I came here for my soon to be sister in laws birthday and fiance, and we devoured so much food. We had 3 people so we were able to order a lot and share. 

For appetizers, we got the mushroom salad, Yum Khai Dao, Goi, scallop ceviche and the uni crab tartlets. The uni tartlets were AMAZING. Pricey but truly an amazing bite. The lemongrass flavor in there was delicious. I also liked the ceviche but wouldn't really get the two salads or tartare again. 

For entrees we got the pork jowl, Bangkok Gai Yang and sea bass chakram. I enjoyed the pork jowl with that garlic rice and the curry with the seabass. The chicken dish was also good and tender but I probably wouldn't get that again since it's pretty similar to the lemongrass chicken I make at home. 

For desserts we got the pandan coconut cake and sweet potato ice cream. Both were good but I wouldn't get these again on a normal day. 

Nothing we ordered was bad - just some things I tried and was ok. Good meal overall and would definitely return!

Before visiting NY, I looked up top Thai restaurants and this place definitely lives up to its name. This was my first time trying an upscale Thai restaurant, I wasn't expecting the place to look so pretty. This was definitely a great place for a dinner date. We were lucky and came at 5pm without reservations on a Friday night with 3 people. Our server was lowkey rude and pushy, but I can't blame him cause all of his recommendations were amazing. He told us that our meal was too meat and carb heavy and recommended the Yum Khai Dao (duck egg salad) and it was tiny but packed with flavor. We ordered the Lin Yang (beef tongue), the Pork Jowl, and the Beef Massaman Curry. If I came back I would order them all again. The Pork Jowl mixed with the crispy garlic and rice was just perfect. And the beef in the curry was so tender and flavorful. Lastly, I ordered the Fish Sauce cocktail and it tastes like a citrus cocktail with a soup broth aftertaste, weird but delicious. Overall awesome Thai restaurant, would recommend!

Amazing friendly bar service and staff. The food was spectacular. Watermelon granita ceviche and sea bass curry were standouts but everything was great and would absolutely order again. The desserts were both interesting and delicious. Cozy upscale but comfortable vibes.

My friend - somehow - was able to get a reservation here and I was ecstatic to *finally* try it out. I had my eye on Bangkok Supper Club as soon as it opened - and I can say that it 100% lives up to the hype. 

We ordered more than we should've, but they were all so worth it! Their scallop ceviche, pork jowl, beef cheeks massaman curry, and ba jang lobster were incredibly tasty with strong, but well balanced flavor profiles. The ceviche was super fresh and the watermelon granita on top took it to another level. All three main dishes were *chef's kiss* and actually ended up being a great selection (thanks to our waiter's recommendation!).

For dessert, they only had the sweet potato ice cream - and I loved it (I'm hoping they expand on their dessert menu soon). It comes with these toasted coconut chips on top and some chunks of cake (tasted like they could've been mochi cake?). Delicious!

Don't sleep on their cocktails either - their guava cocktail was so good (and not too strong). 

Service was excellent as well - super attentive and friendly. Highly recommend!
solid food. smaller portions. pricey. good service. thai food with an American spin with an upscale decor.

Glad I finally got around to coming here! I went to Fish Cheeks a few years ago and have been wanting to try out their new restaurant. I made a reservation a month in advance for a weekday dinner time.

Their cocktail menu is really unique - my friends ordered Beets n' Cream (sweet and creamy, didn't have a strong alcohol flavor), Guava Nam Jim (this one came with a spoonful of fish roe), and Fish Sauce (fairly light, not a strong fish sauce flavorful). For food I think our server recommended one small and one large dish per person - we ended up getting 2 small plates, three large plates, and dessert and that was enough for four of us (though we also weren't super hungry).

For small plates we got Yum Khai Dao (fried duck egg salad) and Lin Yang (beef tongue) which was on the spicy side. Both I thought were just ok. For large plates we ordered the pork jowl, beef cheeks in massaman curry, and the Chilean Sea Bass in chakram curry. The favorite was definitely the pork jowl which was crispy and delicious, would highly recommend getting this. I also liked the beef cheeks, but thought the sea bass was just (I'm a bit picky about curries and I didn't love the flavors in this one). 

We also got both desserts: I loved the coconut one (pandan custard, pandan chiffon cake topped with a coconut cream and with coconut meat on the slides which you can eat as well) and thought the second one was just ok (sweet potato ice cream over a few pieces of rice cakes).

Overall I enjoyed the food but nothing particularly stuck out to me (other than the coconut dessert) and prices were definitely high.
Portions small but highly recommend doing family style! Cocktails were a hit or miss, but Beets n Creme was unique and delicious. Highlights: Sea bass chakram curry, Ba jang lobster and prawn satay

Managed to walk in around 5pm on a Saturday evening last month, so don't fret if it seems impossible to get a resy here! However we were sat at the very corner of the bar so probably didn't get the best experience. It's funny because I'd probably rate this 5 stars if we were anywhere else in the world but by NYC standards, I'd give it a 4. I love Fish Cheeks but BSC didn't exactly *wow* me. It was still very very good though! And service was great.

The scallop ceviche had a kick but was also freezing cold to the mouth so that contrast was very interesting. I think a better dish for the summer. The beef in the massaman was super tender and curry was very rich - delicious overall. We were pleasantly surprised with the portion size of the green bean side - definitely worth it and had a tasty char to them. Branzino was also great, but would like to try other menu items next time.

Service (4/5): Our server felt a bit pushy in terms of having us order more food and more drinks. There were multiple occasions where I pushed the drink menu aside or under the food menu, but the server kept putting the drink menu back on top in front of me. But that being said, he did make some pretty good suggestions that I didn't regret ordering, like the duck egg salad. So I guess overall it's fine. 

Ambiance (5/5): Probably nicest thai restaurant I've ever been to. I feel like they're trying to get their Michelin star especially with the ambiance and plating/decor. Good luck! 

Food (5/5): Massaman curry packed a punch. Very powerful authentic flavors. Beef cheeks were very tender. Pork jowl was cooked to perfection. Beautiful sear + nice and juicy over a bed of garlic rice and  topped with spicy pork cracklings. Make sure to mix it thoroughly and enjoy the combination of textures/flavors! 

Definitely worth stopping by! But note that this will probably be one of the most expensive thai restaurants.
Gotta give it up, 5 stars because BSC hit high notes for service decor ambiance flavor plating and a well-rounded creative menu!

From the moment we walked in, Bangkok Supper Club blew us away with its enchanting ambiance and top-notch service. The atmosphere is both stylish and cozy, perfect for a night out in the city. The staff was attentive, making us feel welcome and guiding us through the menu with great recommendations.

We started with the Pork Jowl with Garlic Rice, which was tender and bursting with flavor. Next, we had the Prawn Satay--juicy and perfectly seasoned, it was an absolute delight. The Scallop Ceviche was fresh and vibrant, offering a fantastic balance of flavors. One of our favorites was the Crab Tartlet--rich, creamy, and simply unforgettable. Each dish was beautifully presented and tasted as amazing as it looked. We also enjoyed two expertly crafted cocktails that complemented our meal perfectly.

Overall, Bangkok Supper Club has won a spot on my list of favorite NYC dining spots. It's a must-visit for anyone looking to experience exceptional Thai-inspired cuisine in a wonderful setting!

Although this place had been recommended but still it exceeded our expectations, the service was friendly and prompt but it was the great food that we all loved, would surely recommend this place for Thai food
Food and service were second to none! Really enjoyed everything we ordered and the drinks as well.

I've been wanting to try Bangkok supper club for a while now, so I was excited to have the opportunity to go tonight.

Service was very friendly, I loved the ambience of the restaurant, and we were seated in a really comfortable booth. The first thing I did was use the restroom, and it was one of the cutest bathrooms I've been in. I loved the tile and aesthetic (I made sure to go twice.)

From looking at the menu, even before I arrived, I was definitely most excited about the large plates. We ordered the duck egg salad, the mushroom salad,   Fried octopus and the Hokkaido scallop. My favorites were the duck egg and octopus, I would probably skip the mushroom salad next time.

The larger plates were the highlight. We ordered the pork jowl, Chilean sea bass, grilled chicken, and green beans. Everything was delicious, and I'd recommend all of the above. Definitely don't skip the green beans.

We ordered both desserts that were available, but I especially loved the Pandan dessert. It was very delicious and itcame with crunchy coconut on top.

Realllyyy yummy food. The pork jowl was my favorite! Flavors were great in that one. I also loved the beef tare tare. My husband loved the octopus as it was deep fried. The prawns were good too but at only 2 shrimps for like $20+ wasn't worth it in my opinion. Didn't get to try cocktails this time around but planning to come back just to sit at the bar. Do get a reservation because they get busy. I would come back for the pork jowl again, it was fantastic. The chicken was good too because of the sauce but it wasn't anything mind blowing. The pork jowl tho - wowwww loved it!

This was excellent. The pork jowl, seabass curry, and scallop ceviche were my favorites, but the ribeye, beef tongue, mushroom salad, and duck egg were also great. I think I prefer Fish Cheeks, all thing being equal, but this was also great in its own way.

Food 5/5 
I had high expectations for this restaurant because it is not a cheap restaurant. The food was great, and it matched my expectations. The cocktails was also quite unique and didn't just contain big ice. Most of us ordered a second drink

Service 5/5
The service was great, and we had a server taking care of us from changing plates to refilling water the entire time. 

Ambiance 5/5
The ambiance was great, and there were a lot of booth seating areas which is great if you come with a group. It feels like a lot of intimate than sitting next to strangers so closely like other restaurants.

Apparently super hard to get res but we just walked in at 430pm and put our name down and got a spot for 630pm! 

Very very flavorful but the small plates are actually kind of small. Octopus was so tender and the dressing was just the right amount of sweet and sour. 

Out of the main plates, pork jowl fried rice is my favorite - so tender and the garlic fried rice is unbeatable. 

Pandan dessert is an absolute must and honestly the main reason I heard about this place !!

Given the price point, fish cheeks maybe more "worth" it.

Amazing. Highly recommend! We loved virtually everything, but our favorites were the pork jowl and the sea bass curry, which was cooked to perfection. The fried duck egg salad was also bursting with flavors. Our least favorite dish was the grilled eggplant but it was still not bad. 

Overall, amazing food with unique flavors all around. Will definitely be back!

Overhyped and over priced.

We got a Saturday night reservation so the restaurant was pretty full. It was quite loud but we made it work without yelling at each other.

Food-
We got the uni/crab tart - mid like maybe a 6/10 if I'm being generous. Mostly people order this for the Instagram.
Duck wrap - honestly the best dish of the night 8.5/10
Lin Yang - it's good but no a wow. Think they could've marinated the beef tongue instead of just pouring the sauce on but that's just one man's opinion.
Pork Jowl - 4/10. Too Rich - WAY WAY too rich. 
Desert - Pandan cake was OK (too creamy)

Overall, overpriced and WAYYYYY over hyped.

Unlikely to come back.

My friend and I went on a Wednesday evening, and managed to get in after around 1-hour wait. The choices of cocktails and food all look innovative with lots of modern combinations but maintain a Thai profile. We started with the uni and crab tartlet and the foie gras duck breast wrap, both are extremely flavorful - one is fresh and the other is rich with lots of umami. Yum Khai Dao is also an interesting salad like appetizer with rich fried duck egg and egg yolk to enhance the flavors. 

The main course we got is the Chilean sea bass chakram curry - impressive flavor and very fresh sea bass. But out of all the dishes, the dessert - coconut pandan pudding, is probably the most memorable and mark a perfect end to this dinner. All the cocktails we had are delicious with clever uses of Thai ingredients as well. The price isn't on the low side for Thai cuisine, but definitely worth to try.

Came here on the heels of a trip to Bangkok. 
The flavors and the vibe took me back to such a wonderful trip.
We had Prawn Satay, Lobster on crispy sticky rice, grilled eggplant and the coconut dessert.

Everything was superb. The service was attentive, friendly, warm and an altogether exceptional experience.
I want to go back!

Truly a tasty experience! Honestly my bf and I ate a lot more but these are all the pictures I got to take. My favorite small bite was the Foie Gras Duck Breast, it's amazing!! My favorite small plate was the Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche. Th texture and mix of ingredients is delicious. The diced watermelon and scallop is such a great mix and it melts right in your mouth. And my favorite large plate was the Bangkok Gai Yang. The grilled chicken is super tasty and it was all so satisfying. I would come here again and again! The ambiance is very relaxed and the place is very popular. Had such an enjoyable time and the staff was very friendly.

Friggin yummy! Is it a bit expensive... sure. Is it worth it? Yes. The pork jowl and Seabass curry were amazing. Oh and must mention to get the crab tartlet! I definitely intend to come back to try other things. And the cocktails are also amazing.

Overpriced Thai tapas? The portions are really small, even for the "large plates." We ordered three appetizers, two entrees, two desserts, and four cocktails, and I could probably still eat more. The prawns--there were only two--were beautifully charred, and the octopus was excellent. My favorite, though, was the beef tongue!

As for the entrees, or "large plates," the Chilean sea bass was amazing--creamy, spicy curry, flaky and full of flavor. The grilled eggplant was just okay, I'd skip it next time. For dessert, the coconut pudding was mildly sweet with a hint of salt--a great combination.

Certainly not your typical Thai spot - no pad Thai or pad see ew found here ! 
I've heard great things about this place previously and it did not disappoint.
Starting with the Yum Khai Dao, I'm usually not a huge fan of salads but this was such a great starter for its refreshing mix of duck egg , yolk and garnish - highly recommend ! 

Scallop ceviche was also clean and tasted fresh , especially combined with the watermelon and mint. Waitress warned us it could be spicy, but personally I didn't find it spicy at all as someone with low tolerance. Just wish there was more! 

Even though they call the entrees "large plates", for the party of 2, the recommendation is 2 small plates and 2 large plates . (They also aren't that large!)

The pork jowl had a nice deep fry and also was tender and juicy, leading to a pleasant combination of textures.

The signature dessert is the coconut pandan ice cream, which was a great way to top off the meal. Recommended, but share that dessert with others because it's deceptively large and can feel quite heavy after a while.
Overall the supper club has gained a new fan and I can't wait to try the other items on the menu!
Excellent Thai cuisine with create. Very good service we love it. Comfortable nice place. Check it out.

Bangkok Supper Club has a sleek, modern ambiance that feels both casual and upscale. The dim lighting and chic decor set a relaxed yet trendy vibe, perfect for a date night or small group gathering. It was a bit on the quieter side, which I appreciated since it made conversation easy without feeling too crowded or rushed.

As for the food, it was decent overall--flavors were good but nothing that really stood out. That being said, the pandan dessert was hands-down the best dessert I've ever had. It was creamy, perfectly balanced, and just the right amount of sweet, making it an absolute must-try. If you go for anything, go for the dessert. 

The atmosphere and friendly service rounded out the experience, making it a spot I'd definitely return to, especially for that unforgettable dessert.

The small plates are perfect for sharing and allow you to try a variety of delicious dishes. From spicy curries to flavorful pork and vegetable dishes, every bite is a delight. The atmosphere is cool and inviting, making it the perfect spot for a delicious night out.

Service was top notch!
The food was amazing but Chef Max and Pat took the experience to the next level. What a treat tonight was. Thank you! We are hoping for a restaurant opening in SF one day.

Ok ok this is up there in the fish cheeks realm! 

For me, Thai is that comfort food but there's so much good Thai in Elmhurst/Jackson Heights area that has real spice and real flavors outside of syrup sweet pad Thai that it's difficult to diverge. 

And then there's the thai that's in cute neighborhoods, a little more on the expensive fancy side, served with mixology programs. A lot of this is done mediocre and almost with too much pronounced flavor, but I think Bangkok supper club does a pretty job at it. I went with a group of friends and they ordered a few things I probably wouldn't order (I like the weird raw shrimp papaya crab stuff as opposed to chicken thigh) 

The flavors were there.

Food
Grilled mushroom salad- i didnt like this and wouldnt order again, theres a texture imbalance. I dont know if the mushrooms were overcooked or intended that way but my jaws hurt from chewing.

Prawn satay- it's just ok. It's enjoyable but not satisfying, feels like something missing.

Octopus
Also nothing to write home about. The octopus wasn't very crispy and felt more doughy.

Pork jowl
The reason i keep coming back. I love this dish but the second time it felt like the portions changed quite a bit. Very little rice, the toppings of pork cracklings and garlic make up 60% of the meal.

Ba Jang Lobster
The lobster was great but the dish is missing something, maybe a good sauce to complete it. It comes with crispy sticky rice and that eats dry with the lobster that doesn't really have a sauce to go with.

Tartare
Probably my least favourite of the dishes. The seasoning was wayy overpowering and made it uneatable.

Desserts
Ive had both and im not a fan of either but the coconut is more interesting.

Service
The atmosphere feels like a fine dining restaurant, it's clear that thats the level of service theyre aiming for. Theres a chefs table and a bar seating area, ive found that you can get easy seats at the chefs table although you will feel the heat from the kitchen and the service is not great. Service is where i feel let down by BSC, and its the little things. The first time i was charged for a sauce without being told it was an extra charge and it wasn't what i wanted so i didn't use it. The second time was my birthday and it wasn't obligatory but would've been nice if they did something small to mark the event, however i got charged for a glass of wine that i didn't order but was brought by the waiter.  I really like the chef however i just think they can do a little more to make it an overall great experience.

Very nice place located near Chelsea Market. Upon arriving, we were seated promptly and were provided a stool for bags. For drinks, definitely recommend the guava nam jim. My partner and I got the Chilean sea bass curry and pork jowl for the main course. Both were very flavorful. Pork jowl was so crispy and melted in your mouth. Moreso than the mains, the appetizers were the star of the day. Definitely get the octopus and the uni&crab tarlet. The burst of flavors were absolutely exquisite.

Was really excited to try this place but I thought it was overhyped.

We did walk in, which some parts of the bar seating are reserved for. Food came out as they were ready, and I thought the seasoning/marinate was what made the dishes unique. They do not have a dessert menu but they do have two desserts, and the one included in my review (forget the name) is the most famous. You sprinkle the toppings as you eat, but I thought it wasn't anything to be wow'ed; just looked nice for pics.

I thought the service was great! He explained to us that it is culturally appropriate to NOT have chopsticks, and the food here is to be eaten with fork/spoon. 

Wish I got to check out the ambiance of the rest of the restaurant, but I never went in deeper than the bar seating.

We scored a Friday dinner reservation and had an amazing experience! 

We ordered the Pork Jowl, and the Seabass Curry for our main courses, and the Beef Tongue (Lin Yang) as our appetizer. The two main dishes seemed to be a popular choice, as our server mentioned this was the combo to get. We loved both dishes, but the Pork Jowl was our favorite! The crispy flakes on the top of the Pork Jowl were so good; it really made the dish for us. The sea-bass was tender and well cooked as well. The beef tongue was just okay, could have probably skipped.

The service was amazing -- our server was friendly, knowledgable about the food, and promptly cleaned up our table after each dish. 

This meal was a tad expensive than our everyday budget, but I'd love to come again to try the other dishes on another special occasion or date night! Highly recommend!

Had dinner here last week with a friend - we scored a 4:30 pm reservation (!) last minute, and when we arrived it was already half full. There were no tables available, so we were seated at a counter in the back, which I actually loved. It felt very private and sequestered and the acoustics were great. 

We started with the crab curry cups topped with uni and caviar, which we ordered at the behest of our server, and she was right: this was maybe the best bite of the night. The creaminess of the crab curry playing off the texture and sweetness of the uni and the crunchiness of the pastry was sublime. 

We followed this with the remarkable scallop ceviche -- which came with a frozen snow cone topping of classic thai flavors (sort of like a green papaya salad) and studded with mandolined slices of raw garlic, basil leaves, edible flowers. This was extraordinary and so refreshing. 

For our mains we split the grilled chicken and sea bass, both excellent. 

For dessert, the pandan cake was only okay -- extremely rich and slightly one dimensional and a mild letdown when compared to the savory dishes. 

I LOVED this experience and will be back. Fish Cheeks is nice, but this is next level.

Walked in on a Friday night after going to The Whitney. Luckily, there was a table available due to the later time. We got three items for three people, an appetizer and two mains. If we were eating at a normal hour, this wouldn't have been enough. However, due to the time it was the perfect amount. 

Yum Khai Dao was a decent salad. I liked the celery leaves and roots. It was balanced with the umami of the duck egg, and the acidity of the tomatoes. My first time having a salad with the base being celery leaves and roots, and I thought it was done well. 

Pork jowl wasn't the most tender than I've ever had. A little bit spicy, and I think the garlic baked rice highlights the spice a little bit more. It was a little bit more one noted than the salad. Beef cheeks Massaman curry was probably my favorite dish. I wanted more beef cheeks in it, but it was quite filling with the rice. 

The dishes are so expensive with a smaller portion than normal Thai places. Definitely a more upscale Thai dining experience. Given my palette, I prefer the bolder flavors of more casual Thai dining places.

Great spot! I came for Resy's 10 year anniversary. The drinks were super innovative and special. The octopus is fully just calamari,'which was a bit misleading or I should've read closer. I really liked the massaman beef curry and the duck egg.

I came here as a party of 4 for dinner tonight. We had an 8:30 reservation but the table before us was taking a while. However, the hosts were super kind and proactive to give us updates, and even offered us their coconut pandan on the house which was so kind of them. 

Once we were seated, we ordered the mushroom salad to start, followed by the beef massaman curry, pork jowl, and sea bass curry. Wow. Everything was so yummy and flavorful. 

The mushroom salad came with a variety of different mushrooms. I honestly don't love mushrooms - it took me like 20 years to start kind of appreciating them - but this salad was delicious. The different types of mushrooms provided a variety of different textures and overall was very light with a bit of tang.

The beef massaman curry was my favorite. It was creamy and the beef cheeks were so tender and juicy. It came with some potatoes and crispy onions as well.

The pork jowl was crisp and flavorful, paired with a spicy rice with garlic crisps. I appreciated the curry sauce to pair as well.

The sea bass curry was also very yummy. I only had a small bite of this one but the fish was tender.

The coconut pandan dessert was also delicious! It was super cute, coming in a mini coconut shell. At first it seemed like just cream with coconut crumbs which they let you pour on top. However, at the bottom there was a coconut cake and coconut meat! It was super light and a great way to end the night.

Overall, delicious food and great service! Would def come back :)

This place is not worth reserving so far in advance, it's mostly hype. So every large dish is mostly rice except the steak. Though I will say what we ordered was tasty, but it was 70% carbs and not very much protein. The sea bass was my favorite flavor wise, but I'd hardly say it's enough to fill 1 person without at least another large plate in addition given that there is so little fish. The pork jowl was very good and had great texture. The beef cheeks had the most meat out of the large plates. I will say that after I mentioned the rice and portion size issue to the manager they did give the dessert for free, but that's not enough to fix the rice and portion problem. I would not come back especially given the price point of the menu.

This restaurant was worth the wait! 
Reservations open up 30 days in advance (though they apparently do leave some seats open for walk-ins). 

Party of 2 on a weeknight at 6 pm. We were both already fans of Chef Max Wittawat thanks to Fish Cheeks and a Platform by James Beard event. 

The space is large and lovely. We may want to try the chef counter seats next time. 

Note that drinks are about $20+ each. We each had a cocktail (mango flame, truffled pandan). I was tempted to order one more Truffle Pandan but I didn't want to spend an additional $21. 

The staff was great! Our server was helpful with our questions and helping decide on portion sizes for 2 people to share. We shared 2 small plates (the server said these are meant to be shared) and 2 large plates, plus 1 dessert.

Everything was presented beautifully and tasted amazing. 

The small plates were great portions for sharing - Yum Khai Dao (fried duck egg) and Grilled Mushroom Salad.


We did wish the Chilean seabass chakram curry had a bigger piece of fish in the curry. The curry itself was a great portion. Other than that, everything had a generous portion size. 

The other large plate we shared was the Ba Jang lobster. We want to come back to try more mains, plus at least one of the Small Bites.

There is no dessert menu. Instead, the server told us the 2 desserts that were offered tonight.  The first was ice cream w sticky rice cake? We went with a coconut pandan cake served in a young coconut. This was PHENOMENAL! I hope they offer this often! It was fun (and delicious!) to scrape the young coconut from the inside of the shell after.

Highly recommend and want to come back!

The place looked really nice and elegant, gave off speakeasy vibes and the service was great, where to they were lacking was the food. Went here for a bday dinner so tried several things on the menu.

Appetizer: fried duck eggs (Yum Khai Dao)- was okay. Bland and honestly didn't taste any different then normal medium boiled eggs. 
-Grilled mushroom salad: pretty good flavor with a slice kick of spice to it
-Fried octopus: amazing! Very well seasoned, crispy and right about of spice with a touch of sweetness. Ended up ordering another one since it was so good. 

Entree: Eggplant: a bit spicy but surprisingly very bland even with her spice but had a nice crisp to it
Chilean sea bass curry: small portion, expected more for $43. Was a small filet of fish drowning in curry. Fish had a nice crisp and curry had great coconut flavor with spice but the fish was done in like 3 bites.
Lobster patty (Ba Jang Lobster): quite delicious, was chunks of lobster over a bed of sticky rice patty, was quite delicious and good quantity of lobster 
Pork jowl: pieces of fried pork cheeks over fried rice. The whole dish taste about the same as pork fried rice from traditional Chinese restaurant, not take out, but authentic Chinese restaurant... meaning it's good and flavorful but not elevated enough for the place or price

Sides: Green beans: nicely charred with some sauce under it that elevated the flavor to something totally different but delicious.

Dessert: coconut chiffon cake- wonderfully delicious! Was a pandan chiffon cake inside a hollow coconut topped with coconut cream. When you scoop around it, can get some coconut meat with the cake which made it refreshing and not too sweet. 

Drinks: I only tried the Tea Tail. Had no taste! Looked and tasted like water down tea with rosemary. Water had more flavor than this tea.
Food was tasty and service was good. Overall felt overpriced compared to what you can get elsewhere.

This place is absolutely fire. I cannot emphasize this enough. I snagged a random Wednesday evening reservation for two people. I had to find someone who would try different thing with me in order to make this experience worth it -- and yes, it was worth it. 

Here's what we got: 
- Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche
- Yum Khai Dao***
- Pork Jowl***
- Branzino

I would get the yum khai dao and the pork jowl again in a heartbeat. Extremely flavorful dishes that made such a difference in our meal. If you're looking for crazy flavor notes, the yum khai dao is the way to go. I can't say I've eaten anything like it.
