I was pretty surprised at how filling it was. Looking at the portion sizes, I was afraid we wouldn't have enough food, but I left feeling stuffed. 

Many of the cocktails sounded interesting, but I wasn't in the mood to drink that day. I would come back with other people who haven't tried Bangkok Supper Club yet!

We came on a Thursday evening without reservations and were seated in about half an hour.  The menu is supposedly Thai street food, but the prices are definitely not street food prices.  Here are some of the items we liked:
* Uni and Crab Tartlet
* Yum Khai Dao (fried duck egg salad)
* Pork Jowl

My husband liked the Lin Yang (beef tongue).  The flavors were good, but I am not a beef tongue person, so did not like the texture purely due to personal preference.  Our waiter recommended the Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry, and I thought it was so-so.  Not only was the fish filet tiny, the curry was just like any other red curry I have had.  It was definitely not worth $43 (1 star off).  Most dishes were flavorful, but pretty salty. 

For dessert, we had a pandan cake which was new to me.  It was a tad salty but surprisingly good that way.  It was a nice dessert to round out the meal.
This restaurant from the outside doesn't look like anything special but once you went in , the environment and the food were extraordinary. Price not cheap though

Really enjoyed dinner at this spot from the Fish Cheeks team. I set a Resy notify and snagged a weekday reservation for three people. We tried:

+ Guava nam jim cocktail
+ Truffled pandan cocktail
+ Coconut aperol spritz
+ Yum khai dao
+ Hokkaido scallop ceviche
+ Beef cheeks massaman
+ Pork jowl 
+ Bangkok gai yang 
+ Bok choy
+ Sweet potato ice cream with sticky rice cake
+ Coconut pandan cake

My favorite things were actually the guava nam jim cocktail and the pandan dessert (the dessert that comes in a whole coconut - super impressive and delicious). Truffled pandan cocktail and pork jowl were excellent, too. Would also recommend the yum khai dao, ceviche and bok choy. Service was great!

4.5 stars.

The food here is just as outstanding as Fish Cheeks, its sister restaurant. 

The pork jowls over garlic rice, uni and caviar appetizer, red curry Chilean bass, and green beans all stood out as stars.

The service was great, nothing to complain about. The vibe is very "cool" and fitting of the west village - loads of younger trendy folks.

We did not have a reservation and got a bar seat for two at the counter when it opened around 5pm. Considering I have been hunting for a reservation for this spot for months, I'll take that as a win.

The Uni and crab was excellent. Was looking forward to the pork jowl, was good but nothing special. 
Had the sweet potato dessert, which was delicious. Good service but server is a little pushy trying to get people to order more.

Solid, upscale thai spot! A good place to bring out of town guests or have a nicer meal.

Came here with a couple of friends on a weekday evening and was able to snag three seats at the bar with no wait.

For food, we tried:
- Lin Yang: Surprisingly tender given it was beef tongue and full of flavor. Would recommend.
- Grilled Octopus: Also very tender and delicious!
- Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche: My favorite dish of the evening! I loved the chili watermelon granita although one of my friends was weirded out by it.
- Green Beans: I really liked this as a green side! The tofu cream added a nice flavor and complimented the charcoal crisp on the veggies.
- Pork Jowl: A solid dish but honestly nothing novel. Similar to pork jowl rice dishes at other thai places.
- Sea Bass Curry: Preferred this main over the pork jowl, the sea bass was well cooked and the curry had good flavor.

Overall, I think the small plates were superior to the large dishes and if I came back would probably stick to just small plates.

Nice interior design and good ambience. Came here with friends for her bday dinner. We like the Bronzino, the crispy pork belly and the curry. Fresh ingredients and decent presentation. Just want to  mention that the dishes are more on the salty side. They do have one hour and half dining time limit, which is not ideal. Overall it was ok but not somewhere I am dying to go back.

Great ambiance but not sure if the food and the price are worth making a reservation a month beforehand.

They have an interesting but pricey menu for cocktails. I would love to try them all if not all of them are at least $20.

The beef tongue and the cod are average. The cod def doesn't worth almost fifty bucks.

The dessert is the highlight of the night. Def recommended. Would come back just for this.

Bangkok Supper Club is a new restaurant by the  team behind Fish Cheeks, which I've never been to due to a lack of veggie options. Bangkok Supper Club also has limited options for vegans/vegetarians, but at least enough for a meal!

We ordered all of the veggie options available:

Grilled Mushroom Salad - Refreshing salad with a nice crunch thanks to the coconut chips. 

Yum Khai Do - This usually comes with trout roe, but they served it on the side to make it veggie friendly. It was good, but not anything particularly special in my opinion. 

Grilled Eggplant (The only vegetarian entree) - The eggplant was well cooked, but I felt it was missing something to make it really stand out. This also has mushrooms, so you're looking at a mushroom heavy meal if you get this and the mushroom salad. 

Green Beans - This is one of two side dishes available (the other is not vegetarian), and it was my overall favorite. The green beans were perfectly cooked and I loved the tofu crema. 

Sweet Potato Ice Cream - They only have two dessert options, so we ordered both. I was skeptical about sweet potato ice cream, but it was so good. Subtly sweet and vegan!

Overall, I'm glad I went. The restaurant is beautiful and our server was amazing. She gave us honest feedback on what/how much to order, so we got a good variety without over ordering. 

They also have a really great cocktail list with a mix of traditional and adventurous options. I likely won't go back to eat, but definitely want to try more of their cocktails.

I went to Bangkok Supper Club recently for a birthday dinner and loved it! The place is well-decorated and very cute. It's giving ~upscale~ Thai.

I shared the Yum Khai Dao (small plate) and Chilean Sea Bass Chakran Curry (large plate). My favorite dish of the night was definitely the Yum Khai Dao! This is a "salad" consisting of deep-fried duck egg with a deliciously jammy yolk, tomatoes, trout roe, grated cured egg yolk, and flavorful herbs! The sauce was what I consider to be "traditional Thai flavors" with fish sauce, chilis, and lime! I had never had a dish like this before so I think that surprised me and made me enjoy this dish most. A must-get!

The Chilean Sea Bass Curry was very good too. I didn't think it was anything too special; it tasted like a good Thai curry with dominant flavors of coconut and chili. The fish was very well cooked, seared well on the outside, and soft/flaky on the inside.

My friends ordered the Grilled Eggplant and the Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche which they thought were wonderful as well. All in all, I think you can't go wrong with anything on the menu here.

Because we were celebrating a birthday, the restaurant brought out a sweet potato ice cream on sticky rice topped with dried coconut. It was quite yummy as well. A very fun way to celebrate because it was topped with a sparkler. The sweet potato ice cream didn't taste too much like sweet potato (?), it had more of a caramelized sugar taste. The creamy ice cream worked well with the sticky rice and crunchy coconut chips.

Overall, good restaurant that serves up yummy food! I think the prices are a bit steep so I'm not sure how "worth it" each dish is but, regardless, I think that your meal will be very delicious!

Amazing dishes curated with high quality ingredients and  serious attention to detail! Pork jowl and green beans were superb, my absolute favs. However, the lobster lacked flavor and was in my opinion, subpar. Ceviche and sweet potato ice cream were unique and packed with flavor. The service here was phenomenal, and the ambiance of the restaurant was beautiful. Sitting at the chef's counter felt slightly removed from the rest of the space, but I loved watching the chef's create each dish. Would come back!

The uni and crab tartlet is a must have, despite the $19 per piece price tag.  The freshness of the uni, crab bf Kalisz caviar, mixed with lemongrass coconut relish, resulted in a very refreshing start to a meal.  

I did some research prior to visiting and ordered the dishes people would recommend.  The Yum Khai Dao salad is worth trying, I never had fried duck egg before, let alone incorporating it into a recipe for a salad.  It's flavorful and interesting.  The prawn satay was just okay.  It came with some sauces, but later on I found out that I was charged $9 for the sauces and chopped chili, but there was no mentioning of the extra charges prior.  It would have been great for the restaurant to mention the charges, as I did not end up using the sauces as the dish itself already came with a thick curry cashew butter sauce.  

The chicken thighs dish was my favorite, the meat was juicy and flavorful with a hint of lemongrass and cilantro.  I also like the charred sticky rice patty that came with it.

I had high hopes for the pork jowl, but the deep fried pork cheeks were so dry and the garlic/spiced pork cracklings were a bit overpowering.  

For dessert, I chose the coconut pandan pudding over the sweet potato dessert.  It's rich, creamy and not too heavy. It's a dessert for someone who likes coconut and pandan.  If you do not like the taste of either, I would recommend ordering the sweet potato one (the server later told me he likes the sweet potato dessert more).  

Overall, this place is worth a visit if you want interesting cocktails and supercharged Thai street food inspired dishes.    The restaurant gives a bit of a resort vibe.

We decided to try Bangkok Supper Club after enjoying its sister restaurant Fish Cheeks. Well Fish Cheeks was good, but this takes creative Thai cooking to a whole new level. Beginning with our two cocktails, everything here was extremely well balanced. And while the flavors are strong, nothing was overwhelming. The two appetizers - a mushroom salad and prawn satay - were both exquisite, with the ingredients truly blending together in every bite. And I really do mean that. Chefs often talk about combining the flavors into a single bite, but here it was extremely important, as some of the more mundane ingredients wouldn't carry all that much weight on their own. I found this quite impressive. The two entrees - charcoal grilled chicken and pork jowel - were equally tasty, while perhaps less nuanced. Overall, this was definitely the most innovative Thai cooking I've ever experienced, and probably my favorite. Anybody who appreciates creative fare should try it.

I was able to grab a resy by booking a month in advance, when reservations released. If you don't, it's not impossible to get a table but it's not easy either. We were excited to try because we love their original sister restaurant, Fish Cheeks!
The ambiance is definitely more upscale than Fish Cheeks. 

We had the uni and crab tart each. It's pretty damn pricey and I wasn't the biggest fan because the crab and Thai spices overpowered all the uni and caviar flavors, but maybe I'm just a purist. The hokkaido scallop starter were very refreshing and spicy but not sure if I was a big fan.
Their entrees were much better than the starter courses! We had the beef cheek massaman curry, pork jowl and garlic rice, crying tiger steak and a side of green beans. My favorites were the curry and pork jowl rice. The crying tiger was a bit overpriced considering about 40% of the 32oz. was pure fat and inedible. It was cooked to a great temperature though. 
As for dessert, loved the pandan coconut dessert!! There was perfect crunch and loved their coconut whipped cream. I would pass on the sweet potato ice cream though, I thought the chiffon cake was pretty dry. 

I enjoyed my experience at Bangkok Supper Club!! It's more modernized Thai food, more like Bangkok flavors rather than traditional. It's not comparable to Fish Cheeks, though, because it's good in its own way.

Food wise - 5 stars, although I would personally describe the flavors as "Thai inspired, American forward." Perfect for a group with varying spice tolerance. 

Atmosphere - good vibes but very loud. Make sure you are feeling extra energetic when you visit the restaurant bc you will need that energy. 

Whatever you do, make sure to get the desserts here.

We just bumped into this place one night and ended up with one of the best meals we have had in Manhattan.  Great food, Since we had no reservation they found seats back where the kitchen staff were preparing food - that was fun. Nice staff, very friendly.

Absolutely perfection! The freshness, the taste and the presentation of each small and large plate. We had the octopus and ceviche for starters and the sea bass curry and pork jowl, the tenderness and mixed of flavors are superb. Then we have the cocktails, deliciously prepared and served. This place a must try in NYC!  Love it and will be back!

My friends and I really enjoyed this meal. Every dish was super flavorful and the meat was cooked just right. The Hokkaido scallop ceviche with watermelon was nicely complex across both temperature and texture - I've never had anything like it. All the large plates were fantastic too. I will say though that the Chilean sea bass curry is on the spicier side. Also the portions are on the smaller end!

Really have to work to get a reservation to get in, but it's worth it. The food and overall experience was fantastic and one of the best meals we had all week in NYC.

The crab with uni was incredible to start, it's pricey at $19, but I think it's worth it and the flavor totally delivers. We didn't get any other starters, but had the grilled eggplant which was nice and loved all the accoutrements on top. The massaman curry was good, but nothing too special.

The highlight was definitely the pig jowl and garlic rice, which as a little bit of a heat kick. It was so flavorful and the pork was incredible.

Service was very good and attentive. I saw two of the owners working the restaurant that evening, which is always a great thing to see. It's worth the hype!

This place is extremely popular these days. There are a limited number of reservations available. I had mistakenly booked my reservation for the wrong week and was only able to get early or late (5pm or 9pm) reservations the night before for a Sunday. 

The venue is medium sized with a lot of booths for bigger parties. It's easier to get a table with a bigger party seems like it. I was sat right away when I got there a few min before my reservation time at 5:30p. The waitress was nice, a bit new so some kinks needed to be worked out but overall a good experience. 

The menu is pretty limited if you have a shellfish or fish allergy with only 3 dishes available to eat. The are no modifications that can be made. For food we got the pork jowl, the beef tartare, the uni + crab tartlet, grilled octopus, eggplant, the lobster, crying tiger, and pandan coconut for dessert. I think overall, the food was prepared well with good seasoning but some dishes felt a little overseasoned/salty at times. However, my favorite was the uni and crab tartlet and the pork jowl. I loved the rice mixture the most in the pork jowl in terms of profile and texture. The pandan coconut seamed to be a favorite for dessert across the room as we noticed during our main course. It was an interesting creation, but was a bit too savory for a dessert for me. 

For cocktails I would recommend the mango flame! It's not very sweet but can taste the mango profile strongly.

The best Thai food I've had in NYC! We didn't have reservations, but the wait for bar seating wasn't long. Turnover is also very quick, finished our meal in around 1 hour. 

Started with the beef tongue and it was delicious. Super tender, and aromatic from the herbs. Both entrees were incredible! I loved the crispy bits from the pork jowl rice, and the chilean sea bass melted like butter. Also, everything has a bit of spice to it here. Overall, this place is delicious and I will definitely be back!

Came for an early dinner and we really enjoyed our dining experience here. Really glad I came here with a group of friends which I highly recommend so you can try several dishes. Everything was very unique and flavorful. Portions were pretty good, we ordered 4 small plates and 4 large plates for a group of 5. The service was great, our waiter gave us great recommendations and always checked on us at reasonable times. The drinks were also pretty good. Would totally come back with friends again!

This place is a must . My fav meal in New York and I come from CA with so much good Thai food . 

Cocktails were very good . Ordered both milk punch cocktails . 1 even had fish sauce . Both very good . Balanced and unique . 

The fried duck salad . Perfect flavor . Fresh veggies . Egg fried perfectly . Fish sauce so well balanced . Excellent unique dish . 

Watermelon scallop ceviche . Once the sorbet melted a bit. It worked. Worked so well . Refreshing . Clean . If u like seafood I recommend ordering . 

Star of the night. Pork jowl. Crispy rice . Perfectly cooked pork . This dish was perfection . I am already craving it

Went for a special occasion and was blown away by the food. The massaman curry and grilled octopus were our two must get dishes of the night. Nothing else disappointed and everything was well balanced and full of flavor. The only downside was service felt a little pushy. They recommended everyone get an app and a main. We were a party of 4 and ordered two apps and three mains and were completely stuffed at the end. The aesthetic is super fun and cool to watch what's going on in the kitchen.

Okay, I know I this place is extremely hot right now and the influencers are going crazy over it. But I hate to say it- it just didn't do it for me.

The ambiance and service were exquisite, genuinely worth the hype. The server was kind, knowledgeable, and attentive despite how busy the restaurant was.

I ordered a mango mocktail, which tasted like watered down mango juice from a can with a hint of lemon juice. Vile.

The appetizer  of octopus was flavorful, and the mixed vegetable with mushrooms was underwhleming. We ordered the eggplant main and the chicken thigh main. Chicken was fatty and charred but not spiced well. 

It seems that the flavor profile of this restaurant is "smoked" or hearty,so you may like that if you prefer it to spicy or rich flavors you usually find at Asian restaurants. 

I will not be returning.

An absolutely amazing date night! I was lucky enough to snag a Friday night reservation for my partner and I, and we loved the experience. The service was top notch, as we were walked through all parts of the menu and given recommendations in each section. And they were able to answer all our questions easily!

Drink-wise, we went with the Truffle Pandam and the Strawberry Toast. Both were super unique and delicious, it was hard to pick a favorite but I will say the Truffle Pandam was unlike anything I've ever had before....!!!!

Our three small plates were all brought out at once. It was a little bit overwhelming BUT all three dishes incredible. My favorite was the beef tongue with amazing texture and paired with a delectable sauce.

We chose to share the pork jowl and WOW! the pork was cooked perfectly and the garlic rice was delicious. The pork cracklin was a great touch.

Really amazing date night, and we plan to come back to try more of their exquisite cocktails and yummy bites.

This was an incredible dining experience from start to finish. It makes sense why the restaurant is booked out for the entire month of availability. The food was spectacular, from the crisp, fresh texture of the grilled mushroom salad, to the hearty depth of flavor in the sea bass chakram curry.

- yum khai dao (duck egg, egg yolk, trout roe on a bed of herbs) - savory yet fresh opener to the meal
- grilled mushroom salad - really solid mix of bitterness from the charred lettuce that balances with the umami from the mushrooms and sweet / sour dressing
- grilled octopus - I could've eaten an entire plate of these myself. This warmer, with a hint of spicy, perfectly matched the two salads 

- pork jowl - super savory, pork was cooked to perfection and rice was very crispy
- Chilean sea bass chakram curry (w a bowl of rice) - fantastic, the fish was INCREDIBLE, soft and flavorful, and the curry complemented the sea bass perfectly
- green beans - had to get a vegetable for the meal! Quite interesting with the usual savory green beans served with a lighter, cooler tofu cream

Service was great, food came out in a reasonable amount of time. It was a little loud in the restaurant, but otherwise it's a beautiful setup inside.

Bonus points for those w allergies - as I understand it, they're a peanut free kitchen, and it was really easy to order around my tree nut allergy.

Hands down one of the best restaurants I've been to in NYC. Service was great - we were seated a bit later than our reservation, but our server was fantastic and took the time to explain each dish to us and provide great recommendations based on what we liked.

Food was outstanding - every dish we had was so so good. So worth the hype!! Favourite dish was the pork jowl, but honestly everything was just so good. My friends and I all loved each dish.

The restaurant was beautiful as well. It was very well decorated, super clean, and looked elegant. Can't recommend this place enough!!

Bangkok Supper Club summed in one word: unexpected. I did not expect to fall in love with the mushroom tartlet, which was filled with a burst of of truffle, combined with the most decadent sauce. Unexpected was the pandan dessert, arriving in a coconut filled with a delightful mix of textures and mildly sweet flavors. I am not ashamed to say that my table ended up getting another one to share. After trying most items on the menu here I'm almost confident that you can't go wrong. Among my favorites where the whole branzino, the cauliflower appetizer, the curry, the chicken accompanied by the crispy sticky rice, and the mushroom salad. 

Environment: Perhaps it's the name that made me expect a more dark, loud, and "clubby" environment, but I was pleased when I walked in and was greeted by the most cozy, warm, inviting atmosphere. Not to mention, the serving stuff here are absolutely incredible. 

Bangkok Supper Club did not disappoint one bit.

Omg yall - so all in all great food and service - run don't walk. Look at the pics/vids and order the same exact things. Add the branzino to your order though. I ordered it but he didn't hear me. 

The long version - 

I found out this was Fish Cheek's sister restaurant a couple of days before coming. So I was super excited. I really enjoyed the food at the fish cheeks - the service not so much (we sat at the bar). 

We ordered - 

1. UNI AND CRAB TARTLET - this is the most delightful thing have tasted in a while. It takes awhile to get to the blue crab but once you do all of the flavors start to come together. 
2. FOIE GRAS DUCK BREAST WRAP - I thought this was going to be a paté but I was pleasantly surprised by the actual sliced meat. I didn't see what was underneath it but another flavorful dish. 
3. GOI - an interesting spin on beef tartare. Not memorable. 
4. PRAWN SATAY (pictured, but I didn't try)
5. HOKKAIDO SCALLOP CEVICHE - this wasn't my favorite. I'm also not a huge ceviche fan. My friend is and she loved it. 
6. PORK JOWL - this would be my favorite dish after the tartlet. Just excellent. 
7. BEEF CHEEKS MASSAMAN (pictured, but I didn't try)

Cocktail: GUAVA NAM JIM 

We arrived at 6pm with no reservation and snagged seats at the bar - Danny assisted us. He was great. Made the experience that much better.

We needed a place to go after a late night at the Whitney. It was a Friday night and we didn't have a reservation. They only had seats at the bar by the kitchen. What a treat! 
I started with the: OKKAIDO SCALLOP CEVICHE "Sashimi grade Hokkaido scallop, pickled watermelon rind, diced watermelon, mint and garlic, topped with chili watermelon granita." it was amazing. Maybe one of my new favorite dishes. 
For a main I had:
BA JANG LOBSTER
Sautéed Lobster in brown butter, served over aromatic black pepper sticky rice garnished with Nasturtium leaves and garlic chips.
Also really great.
My friend and I shared the : GREEN BEANS, "Charcoal grilled green beans, sweet peas and English peas, crispy garlic chili oil, tofu cream and crispy shallot."
We had the dessert that came in a young coconut.
It was a unique and delicious culinary experience. I highly recommend sitting at the bar. It was an extra treat to watch the chefs make their magic, but it was still comfortable enough for an easy dinner conversation. I can't wait to go back!

There is no limit in terms of overpriced food in manhattan accommodating mediocre food. Bangkok supper club is one of them. 
If you are looking for authentic and true Thai flavor Thai food, this is not for you. The chef seems to incorporate American flavors to some Thai dish but the flavor is very strong , and the longer you eat, the more you felt like it is just too much(too dense that I felt like throwing up) 

In my humble opinion, Thai flavor should be refreshing, and lightful. But here, I felt like everything is heavy and the way it combined together is making things worse. 
I do know ppl can be appreciate it on this restaurant's and chef's creativity. However, I am a dedicated fan who always respect the originality of each of the cuisine. 
I mean, I see few chefs that can cook decent original flavor of their so-called xx cuisine. But the market is just embracing the fusion flavor due to eaters? 
I guess that is the reason so many good restaurants are closing whereas you see high prices of non sense exisiting. What a market.
Loved our meal here. The curry fish was amazing highly recommend. Service was impeccable. The chicken was delicious. We also had the prawns, bokchoi and beef tartar.

My wife and I were so excited to try this place and left very disappointed. On the positive side, the place has a good ambiance - lively and energetic for sure although I didn't get any "Bangkok/Asia" type feel. Our server wasn't good at all - started out well but then disappeared for long stretches. Didn't alert us to the spiciness of some of the dishes until after they arrived. Forgot my wife's birthday and when I mentioned he didn't put a candle on the dessert he couldn't even apologize. The food itself was ok - hit or miss but we were surprised it was as spicy as it was. Given the prices there are better places. I did express my disappointment to the GM Paul who wrote a nice note back but we aren't interested in going back there.

The service and ambiance are top notch and fun, however, where it falls short is the food.

From my Thai dad who joined us for a meal here, "This place is for young hip people who want to waste money. I think the cook in the back might be Mexican. The curry and sauces seem premade." 

I personally found the food underwhelming and only liked one item we ordered. Everything was way too salty and lacked the flavors I'd expected from a Thai restaurant.

What we ordered:
1. Octopus (3/5): Good, not great. Octopus was chewy and not tender. It was overcooked. Flavors were good.
2. Hokkaido Scallops (3/5): Really enjoyed the flavors. The scallops were fresh and delicate. However, the texture of the granita was not good. There were too many large chunks of ice and it did not complement the delicate nature of the scallops. My teeth were hurting.
3. Pork Jowl (2/5): I really didn't like this dish at all.
4. Beef Cheeks (2/5): I also didn't like this dish as a whole. The beef was tender, which was good. But the flavors were completely missing. The dish was quite bland. (I'm eating this right now as leftovers and I've added additional spices. It's a huge improvement.) 
5. Sea bass Curry (3/5): Sea bass was cooked well and it was fresh. What was lacking yet again was the flavor. I liked how it was spicy, but that was about it.
6. Gia Yang, aka chicken (5/5): This simple dish was my favorite since the chicken was extremely juicy and tender, also the sauce that came with it was authentic. However, it being $38 is not worth the price.

Service: 5/5
Food: 4/5
Ambiance: intimate, lively

Lives up to the hype! Atmosphere is on the nicer end, we'll trained staff and thoughtful dishes. Menu has good variety without being overwhelming. Next time I want to try for kitchen bar seating.

What I Ordered:
- Scallop Ceviche: mouth felt like fire + ice, fresh scallops but the sweetness was overpowered by the spice.
- Pork Jowl: tender, cooked to the point right before it could've been considered dry. flavorful rice. slightly spicy.
- Grilled Eggplant: good, but underwhelming compared to the other dishes. sweet, not at all spicy
- Pandan Chiffon Cake: not too sweet, beautiful presentation

Wow, my favorite new restaurant in a while. 

The pork jowl is a must order; the scallop ceviche, prawn satay, fried octopus, and beef cheek curry were also incredible. Dessert was the only department I wasn't too impressed by, but I'd truly reorder all of the other dishes 

Already looking forward to my next visit!

Finally managed to get a reservation here and it was well worth it. We enjoyed everything we ordered, but some highlights were the Hokkaido scallop ceviche - very unique flavor and texture combo - and the grilled eggplant! All of the other mains we tried were pretty solid and super flavorful - pork jowl, both curries and the chicken thigh. The space is pretty spacious, modern, and nicely decorated. Service was friendly and attentive. Save room for dessert. We ordered both the sweet potato ice cream and pandan coconut cake, which were refreshing and a great way to end our meal.

Bangkok Supper Club is for sure one of my new favourite restaurants that I will be recommending to all my friends. Rarely do I ever want to return to a restaurant in New York but I can't wait to go back!

All the food that we ordered is delicious and reasonably priced for the portions. Our waitress was so sweet and took her time in suggesting dishes by even further explaining the flavours of her favourite dishes. 

The atmosphere is not to be overlooked either, the interior is beautifully modern and the back has an open kitchen concept with bar seating.  

Overall, this place is totally worth the hype and I will definitely be back for a special occasion!

New fave Thai spot if you are looking for higher end cute date. Every dish felt unique and was very well flavored. It looks like the biggest table could fit 4-5 ppl so I would be that in mind as the largest group size.

TLDR: Bangkok Supper Club is another project from the team that brought Fish Cheeks. This is a bit more buttoned up, more elaborate dishes and a fantastic cocktail program. Duck Egg Salad, tartare and those prawns!

It was very difficult to grab this reservation but we were able to finally try BSC. The restaurant is very clean, nicely put together, definitely more polished than Fish Cheeks.

The cocktails we had were very tasty, I can't remember which ones but they were delicious.

Food. The duck egg salad I enjoyed very much. Salty, crunchy, lots of texture and not something you'd find on most Thai menus. Satay prawns were good especially with the char and all of that sauce. The tartare was excellent, definitely one of the better larb-esque dishes. 

The sea bass curry was good but I probably like the crab curry from FC a bit more. The pork jowl fried rice was good but if you've had a good garlic fried rice before, it does start to get a bit one-dimensional after awhile. Especially if it's two people splitting it. It's a pretty dish though.

Coconut dessert was plated really well and tasty. I appreciated the coconut as the serving vessel, the cake and the young coconut meat as well.

I enjoyed BSC and will definitely be back, especially for the drinks. If you had to make me pick though, I probably like Fish Cheeks a bit more. The flavors are a bit more punchy, in your face and I like that. Bangkok Supper Club is great too but definitely more showcasing more technique and texture.

We managed to get a reservation for 5pm, right as they opened. The place was already packed when we got there so I would definitely recommend making a reservation.  The service was friendly, attentive, and quick all evening. The food was amazing all around, we didn't order one dish that wasn't great. The drinks were a bit hit or miss, and can be skipped. The fried egg and watermelon ceviche small plates were definitely the most flavorful. We had 4 people and got one of everything on the small plates menu, and then 2 large plates. I would def recommend as many small plates as you can handle. Overall, absolutely worth the hype and can't wait to come back.
Amazing!!! Absolutely loved all the dishes we got. The uni appetizer was amazing and the drinks were so delicious. Staff was great, ambiance great, will be returning!

My part of four had a reservation at 7:30 we made prior to dining - pro tip run and grab a res now! They turned away a bunch of people at the door with an almost 3 hour wait for a table for walk ins! We ordered some drinks (our favs being their beets 'n' cream) and each ordered a small plate and entree as recommended by their staff. 

For small plates, we ordered their Yum Khai Dao, Hokkaido scallop ceviche, Lin Yang and grilled octopus. Everything was so flavorful and we literally could not find any fault aside from wishing there was more. For entrees, we ordered their pork jowl, beef cheek masaman, ba jang lobster, and Bangkok gai yang. Again, amazing flavors and texture profiles! Their curry and pork jowl packed a light kick as did the dipping sauce for the gai yang. All of the meats were cooked to perfection!! They didn't skimp on the lobster (which comes without the shell!) we loved every dish we ordered and the sticky rice that accompanied the chicken and lobster! For dessert we ordered both their coconut pandan cake and their coconut sugar ice cream. Both had notes of coconut with the coconut pandan cake being a lighter more fragrant coconut flavor and the ice cream really packing in a sweeter richer coconut flavor. 

Overall, it's a gorgeous and lovely space with great food, drinks and service. Definitely worth a try for a more upscale Thai dining experience!

Cute spot, reservation were hard to get but space was 1/3 empty when I dined there.

Sea Bass Curry is better than Beef Cheek Curry.

Grilled Chicken and Pork Jowl both comes with rice, pretty good but safe dishes.

White Asparagus & Snap Pea Salad sides were on the bland side, missing a flavor kick, but has the texture.

Mushroom Salads ended up being the most spicy dish, in a good way.

Prawn Satay is delicious.

Cocktails were fun and creative with asian flavors.

Waitress was super passionate on explaining the dishes, making everything sounds extra delicious.

Overall a really great experience! If you come early you can get a walk in, but it's tougher later. I found the lobster and beef tongue dishes to be stellar. Packed with flavor and really tender. The sea bass and massamune curry were just okay. All in all, great experience though!

I can't even begin to express how much my group enjoyed our dinner at Bangkok Supper Club. We came on a Saturday evening at 5:30PM for my birthday. The restaurant itself gives chill, tropical vibes, including the bathroom! 

Nearly everything we ate and drank was outstanding, 20/10. Our server was great, she was attentive and went through all the various dishes with us. 

The one thing I did not like was that the "small bites" are literally one piece each. That should probably be noted on the menu so you don't end up spending $60 on one bite for multiple people. 

My favorites of the night included the large plates: Pork Jowl with garlic rice and cracklings, the Chilean Sea Bass over Chakram Curry with jasmine rice, and the Grilled Chicken with sticky rice patty. Everything was DELICIOUS and so crave-able. I am still thinking about this meal nearly 2 days later. All the sauces and spices on top of varying rice dishes was so comforting and the perfect combination- slightly spicy and mellowed out by the rice. I was really surprised at how much I loved the Chilean Sea Bass. I am not a fish person, but it was cooked so perfectly and it was so delicate. That curry sauce was next level. 

I also really loved the dessert, especially the coconut pandan one. It was served in a giant coconut with chiffon cake, actual coconut meat, toasted coconut, and some sort of cream. It was light and the perfect ending to a very flavorful, spiced meal. 

Our drinks were spectacular. I had various tequila and mezcal-based drinks, they were sweet and fruity and well balanced. 

I don't normally go back to restaurants, but I am totally in love with Bangkok Super Club.

Loved Bangkok Supper Club. Walking in, it doesn't feel like a Thai place. Very modern and chic. 

The food was very good. Some dishes missed like the lobster but majority of them had some very nice bites. 

BSC felt like a fancy spin on some traditional dishes, but I thought they did it well. 

Would def come back if reservations are easier to get.

I was super excited to try this restaurant because I heard it was Fish Cheek's sister restaurant. Ambiance was super chic and service was amazing. 

However, I wasn't that amazed by the food. Felt like the prawns itself were bland but the curry it came over was pretty good. The desserts were just alright, so that was disappointing

One the best meals I have had in recent memory. Every dish was excellent but what stood out to me was: the scallop ceviche small plate (devine bit with good heat), the whole Brazino (visually memorable presentation) and the pandan pudding dessert (shareable but you must like coconut). Portions were just right and flavors were unique. Service and decor were both excellent. Highly recommend.

This was the best dinner I've had in a while. We had a reservation and were sat immediately (it's difficult to get a reservation but we noticed a few unoccupied tables so try to walk in!). The staff was extremely professional and courteous and the service throughout the night was excellent. The food was amazing and so well executed.

We ordered:
- Mango Flame mocktail - yummy. Smoked Tea cocktail - just ok.
- 2 Uni and Crab Tartlets. Probably the best bite we had all night and everything was incredible! Silky and fresh, so tasty.
- Goi. The beef tastes flavorful, fresh and slightly spicy, and we loved the spice on the puffed rice chips.
- Pork Jowl with Garlic Rice. The rice managed to outshine the pork in this dish - great texture from the fried garlic.
- Bangkok Gai Yang. Perfectly cooked chicken thigh with a delicious earthy lemongrass flavor, combined with a bright and tangy sauce and charred sticky rice. Chef's kiss, so mf good. 
- Coconut Pandan Pudding. The pudding inside the coconut is good, but combined with the young coconut meat elevates this dish to the next level! Loveddd this dessert so much.

Overall I would save this restaurant for a special occasion as it is quite pricey! But soooo worth it. I can't wait to go back.

It sounds like you had a wonderful experience at Bangkok Supper Club The cocktail menu must have caught your attention with its interesting options, and the Mango flame kick it very refreshing my friend  she love beet and cream . I love that they have an open kitchen as excellent service can truly enhance a meal.Ours server Pat she incredible !!!  she recommended all dishes and drink  very delicious and flavor  now im will be the big fan of Bangkok supper club.
The cozy atmosphere also sounds inviting. Bangkok Gai Yang  it's tender and i love  the egg sticky rice  and the sauce ,im not the big fan of grilled fish but the brazino kill it ....
i try to make reservations for next time but very difficult all full booked
5star

Start from the first impression when I step in the host team a very warm, welcome atmospheres very cozy clean I ordered a Hokkaido scallops, are incredible with watermelon Amazing favor the prawn satay  they do the homemade cashew nut butter is totally different from another Thai restaurant over all total whole meals, five star talk about the Service. The service is very excellent Pat she is my server keeps touching all the night. she explains all the favor of the food where traditional if you need any success anything about the food and Thailand,I highly recommend to ask her service.

My first time here  my experience was amazing 
 I ordered yum kai dao.  With 3kind egg very delicious 
Pork jowl kill  everything  and dont forget to ask for dessert when you arrive  coconut pandan they have limited every night. Pat was amazing keep touching the table and good recommend
I sat at the bar the drinks and food was amazing. I love everything I ordered and will go back for sure !!!

In short, mostly great food with a great atmosphere and great service, but pricier than many other restaurants of its type.

Small plates:
1. Yum khai dao (duck egg salad) -- the duck egg itself was delicious, the rest of the salad was good enough and tasted like typical Thai salads
2. Lin yang (beef tongue) -- not very flavorful but will note I've never eaten beef tongue that I loved

Large plates:
1. Pork jowl -- this was amazing; the rice had a good crunch to it and was presented very nicely
2. Beef cheeks massaman -- a very tasty massaman curry; tastes as you'd expect but in a good way, texturally fun thanks to the roasted shallots and pairs perfectly with the Jasmine rice that is cooked well
3. Bangkok gai yiang (grilled chicken) -- delicious chicken that's tender; portion size is large. The sauce that came with it didn't have as much flavor as I expected, but it was already seasoned well enough by itself. Comes with a sticky rice patty that's unique but doesn't offer much over sticky rice alone (though it's cut into 4 so easy to share!)
4. Ba jang lobster -- the worst of the group in my opinion; the lobster was fine and the sticky rice situation was similar to that of the chicken. To be clear, this isn't bad lobster at all, just nowhere near as exciting or flavorful as the other items we ordered.

Dessert:
1. Pandan coconut cake -- served in a young coconut, this was the highlight of the meal. A delicious cake with real coconut is wonderful both taste- and texture-wise. As a bonus, once you finish eating the cake, you can scrape out the coconut meat lining the inside which is still coated slightly with the flavors of the cake. Beautiful, fun, and delicious!
Beautiful restaurant and thoughtfully curated tasty food. Our server Pat was absolutely a sweetheart. Incredibly thorough and attentive. We appreciate you!

Went to BSC this Valentines Day because of all the great reviews. Had a pregnant friend with us who was told no substitutions could be made for pregnancy, but they would let us know which foods she couldn't eat, but charge her the full price for items she couldn't eat. Minimum spend was $600 for 4 people (receipt attached), but what they did not tell us at reservation was what was on the "special Valentines tasting menu" beforehand. We left hungry because they served two portions of everything for 4 people. For example, 1 scoop of the ice cream dessert per couple. Made me wonder if they were serving half a scoop of ice cream for a single person who decided to dine alone. One main dish per couple, and so on with drinks separate from the minimum spend, so a whopping $900 for a dinner, which we had to supplement with casual food at a different restaurant afterwards. 

I am a seasoned New York City diner and this restaurant did not provide any value for cost. Maybe the experience is different on regular days without a special menu, so beware going here on special events/holidays.

The service provided by Melody was EXCEPTIONAL!!!  She was friendly, remembered everyone in my parties name, explained everything on the menu and guided our choices.  

Loved the food!!  Everything was flavorful and great portion size. We had the octopus. Scallops, crab tartlet for starters. Our entrees were steak, garlic rice with pork, Bronzino and charred Bok Choy....everything was a 10. 

I also liked when the servers brought the food to the table they were also very informative. 

All in all it was an amazing experience. My recommendation is request Melody....you will receive phenomenal service!!
Amazing presentation and great service! We love it here. Should be a 10/10. This was our NY eve pre meal and it was fantastic and love the manager and friendly staff.

Very pretty interior
Good for birthdays, regular get together dinners, celebrations
The service here is friendly and attentive but they do keep you to your dining time limit. The food here is delicious but very expensive; I believe an entree is between $45-$52. For the 4 of us we got 2 entrees, 2 veggies sides, 1 appetizer, 1 cocktail, 2 mocktails, 1 pot of tea and 2 desserts and that came out to $330 with tax and tip. I'm glad I finally got to try this hotspot but it's not a restaurant I'd put in my regular rotation

For quite some time this place is one of the hottest reservations in NYC and finally, we had dinner here. The food, drinks,  and the atmosphere clearly explained the craze. The cocktails we ordered were prompt and enjoyable. To start with we ordered the 'Uni & Crab Tartlet' from the small bites and the "Prawn Satay' from the small plates. Both were phenomenally good.  From the large plates, we ordered "Pork Jowl", "Grilled Eggplant" and "Ba Jong Lobster". For us, the Pork Jowl was the crown jewel of the night, especially due to the delicious garlic fried rice that came with it. We devoured every single piece of rice from the bowl.  The eggplant was also very tasty. However, the lobster was a bit let down mainly due to the bland sticky rice that came with it.  Our servers were super friendly and prompt. One final comment, the host at the entrance didn't have to greet the guests in a stern voice that the table was needed back in 2 hours. In no restaurant of this class in NYC, a dinner takes more than 90 minutes & we took even less than that. That first greeting at the restaurant left a bad taste.

ok i see the hypee.. the food was SO GOOD but i will say their price point is fairly high for the portions (small so we  shared 4-5 dishes for three people)

get the beef cheek massaman curry & pork jowl!! 
people have mixed reviews about the chicken but we truly enjoyed it + the rice was nice and crispy (so maybe it depends on the day)

the chilean sea bass curry was good but not my fav, neither the beef tongue which personally i found a bit tough. but to each their own cause my friend loved both!!

get the pandan coconut dessert, literally mindblowingly good and converted me to a coconut lover!

It really is that good!! Went to Bangkok Supper Club without a reservation on a rainy Sunday evening at around 6:15 and put our names on the waitlist for bar seating. After enjoying a glass of wine across the street at Lavaux, we were called at around 7.

I'm happy to report the hype is real! This was probably one of the more delicious meals I've enjoyed in NYC. Here's what we ordered:

- uni and crab tartlet: this was SO good, one of my favorite dishes. the uni was so fresh and oozy and it was delicious with the sweet and creamy crab/tart. next time I want to try supplementing with caviar. 

- foie gras duck breast wrap: took a tiny bite of this, it was just ok. if you've never had mieng khan, it's a leaf with an assortment of sweet and crunchy nuts/seeds. pretty good but nothing crazy. the duck could've been a little warmer for me. 

- yum khai dao: this is the fried duck egg salad and it was so delicious and fresh! super unique textures with the deep fried egg and assorted crunchies. be careful, it is quite spicy.

- hokkaido scallop ceviche: the scallops were great in here, but the dish was a little too cold/icey and sweet for me. I probably wouldn't get this next time. 

- pork jowl: get this!!!!!!! my favorite dish of the night, the pork was cooked so perfect and the rice was packed with flavor with delicious crisps of garlic and pork cracklings. I don't normally like meat as much as I do seafood, but this jowl was excellent. 

- chilean sea bass chakram curry: tender sea bass in red curry. this dish had the perfect amount of spice and the fish was cooked very well. it was a very good curry, but wasn't a standout; tasted like a pretty standard red curry. I think I kept comparing this dish to a similar dish I've had recently, but with scallops instead of sea bass, so it wasnt particularly novel to me. 

- coconut pandan cake: despite being stuffed to the brim after all the aforementioned food, we were convinced to get the coconut pandan cake served in a coconut and are we glad we did! I definitely made room for this. coconut cake with pandan pudding and chunks of jelly, topped with fresh whipped cream and a side of toasted coconut. this was a little on the sweet side but soooo good

Overall, loved my experience at Bangkok Supper Club. Not overhyped at all! Can't wait to be back and try the cocktails.

My group of 4 had a fantastic dinner experience here. When you walk in, there's a little waiting room by the hostess with a bench while you wait for your party to get seated. Inside is nicely decorated - not stuffy or too casual. The general manager Paul was very friendly and introduced himself to us once we sat down. My friend also saw Dominique Ansel dining the same time as us and is a huge fan so Paul was nice enough to let us know it would be okay for my friend to approach him for a picture and also made his waitress aware. 

Onto the food - everything we ordered was phenomenal. For small plates, we ordered the Yum Khai Dao (fried duck egg salad) and Lin Yang (beef tongue). For mains, we ordered the pork jowl, ba jang lobster and Chilean sea bass chakram curry. Everything had delicious and unique flavor. 

I can't wait to come back here to try more dishes! Everything from the atmosphere to the service and food was perfect for a dinner with friends.
We came here because we love this sister restaurant fish cheeks. The food is okay but I would keep going back to fish cheeks

Americanized Thai but very nicely done! Think I will go again to try other dishes and the coconut cake. Walked in as 2 with no wait on a Thursday night at 7. 

The miss: grilled octopus has a bitter garlic-y flavor that's too bold for octopus; the strawberry cocktail tastes disjointed/artificial, and the bar tender didn't offer to take it off the bill. I clearly ordered and finished a different drink but left strawberry alone. 

Liked: pork jowl over rice mixed with crispy shallots. Meat tastes great, but they could cut back on the shallots a bit. 

Loved: the scallop ceviche with watermelon, spicy and sweet; beef tongue was perfectly tender and flavorful; the juicy chicken meat with a nice touch of separating the skin, getting it charred and placed back on top of the chicken; ice-cream and the beet vodka + cream cheese cocktail are both excellent choices for those who want a small dessert.

Extraordinary food that I have ever tried. The drink is perfect. The staff is splendid, especially Pat, who has an excellent service mind, and when it comes to the menu lists, Pat did a great job explaining the dishes. Recommend for everyone to come and experience this excellent restaurant.

This was maybe one of the best meals I've ever had. Pat gave us absolutely phenomenal service. For apps we did a mushroom salad, scallop ceviche and beef tartare everything was DELICIOUS. Main course we got pork jowl (waiter said he would lay down his life for it), a chicken situation, and sea bass curry - I can't even pick a favorite. Between the food and Pat's service I cannot recommend enough!!!
literally amazing food maybe even better by our amazing server Pat!! We will be back!

I don't know how many time my Thai friends have told me about the Bangkok Supper club. However this place made me super surprised and ya'll got my first impression of thai food in NYC. I could even say it is one of a kind of greatest Thai restaurant, comparable, substantial portions, great vibes and the service was on top of everything. Majority, servers are very friendly, attentive. They all got a big smiles on their faces, Love it!

My dinner was in little rushed to hit to other place but the dinner was a memorable. My dinner served in time manner and amazing presentation but food way too sweet. Especially coconut milk  dishes such as curry. The spiciness was extremely perfect of being  authentic Thai food. 

I was seating by myself at bar top and I just realized ya'll have also the best beverage menu in town. The menu is not being that huge and stunted you until you won't know what to eat!

Service 9/10
Ambiance 10/10
Foods & drinks 10/10

I would definitely go back and you folks must  try out! 

www.explorekissaki.com

I now understand why it's so difficult to get a reservation here. If you're lucky, you'll either score a 5pm or 10pm dinner reservation  

Our group of 4 ordered almost everything on the menu:
- Bok Choy 
- Goi (tartare) 
- Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche
- Lin Yang (beef tongue) *favorite*
- Pork Jowl over garlic fried rice *favorite*
- curry sea bass
- Bangkok gai yang (grilled chicken thighs)

I love how well lit this place is and the open kitchen. Don't forget about their cocktails!

Best choice to celebrate my friend's birthday. Really cool vibe with elevated Thai cuisine and great cocktails. The Hokkaido scallops is the best, super refreshing and creative. Sea bass curry and beef tartar are also the must! Will def' go back there again!

My husband and I booked tickets for the New Year's Eve dinner at Bangkok Supper Club. We were already fans of Fish Cheek and wanted to check out this new spot. Our first impression was that the place is very modern, sleek, and infused with Thai style. As a Thai person, I always seek authentic yet creative food experiences.

For the first course, we had Uni and Caviar with coconut sauce and king crab--it was amazing. Everything melted in my mouth. There were so many courses that we can't describe them all. The drinks were different and complemented the food perfectly. Our server, Mint, greeted us in the sweetest way and took care of us like we were part of the family, yet remained professional.

We had the opportunity to say hi to the owner and chef, who were nice and explained the details about their food. After New Year's, we went back again, bringing my sister from Thailand to visit. Once again, all the food was fantastic. I highly recommend Bangkok Supper Club.

It is my first time here. Although I didn't have reservation but finally I got a good spot at the bar. The drinks are so good. Thanks both server and bartender for advicing. Love the vibe. I could be here all night. Definately recommended!!!

TLDR: An absolute must try for upscale Thai cuisine. 

The uni crab tartlet was an absolute sensation - it melted in my mouth, and the caviar topping, generously provided on the house, added the perfect pop of flavor. Creamy and irresistible, it left me craving more.

The crying tiger rib eye showcased perfect cooking, with an insanely tender texture. The accompanying tomato tamarind mash added a lovely touch, and the spice kick elevated the steak to new heights. A truly satisfying dish for steak enthusiasts.

The star of the meal, however, was the chicken with crispy rice. I haven't tasted chicken this tender and juicy in a long time. The depth of flavor in both the chicken and the perfectly paired sauce was truly impressive. I would return to Bangkok Supper Club just for this exceptional dish.

To end the meal on a sweet note, the pandan cake dessert was a unique and perfect choice. It provided a sweet bite with a hint of crunch, rounding off the dining experience on a high note.

My friend and I had a reservation for 2 at 7:30pm on a Friday so we got quickly seated and the ambience was great. The seats were extremely close to one another so we could barely hear each other speak. We ordered a small bite - the crab, uni, caviar bite and it was delicious. they had free caviar that night and I'm usually not a fan of uni but the flavors balanced so well. We also got the Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche, which was refreshing but spicy, and the Sea Bass Curry as our entree. the fish was cooked so well and it was a big piece, and the flavors of the curry was great. The portions were fair and they recommended a small and large plate per person but we wanted to save room for dessert. The sweet potato ice cream (vegan) paired so well with the coconut flakes and sticky rice cake. Overall great experience, it was just pricey!

You know when you love your friend, so you know you'll love their friends? That's how I feel about Fish Cheeks--I knew I'd love any of its younger siblings. And I did like BSC--I just didn't love the prices.

For appy apps, we shared the Yum Khai Dao, which was complex and delicious, and the Goi, which was gorgeous and flavorful. The Goi portions were fine, but the Yum Khai Dao was Yum Too Small for me, personally. I could've done with about twice more for that price point.

My favorite thing at Fish Cheeks is probably the Pork Jowl, so of course I had to get the glow up version offered at BSC. It was lovely and the cracklings were on point, but again, I could've done with a bigger portion. Cue Zoolander, "What is this, a cheek for ANTS?!" That kinda thing.

The Bangkok Gai Yang was succulent and juicy, but the side of charred sticky rice patty was burnt and unnecessary. At least season the rice if you're going to serve something like that. The same annoying patty made a reappearance when we added on the Ba Jang Lobster because we were still hungry. This time, it sat underneath an otherwise great dish--think rice pizza topped with perfectly cooked lobster and my favorite herb to mispronounce (nasturtium). Personally, I could've done without the rice. 

Sometimes, a meal gives great foreplay but no payoff--aka great apps/entrees but lackluster dessert. Fortunately, Bangkok Supper Club adhered to the "Bang" in their name (I know, I know, but I couldn't help it) because we concluded with a dessert that made us need a pack of cigarettes. Said dessert was a Pandan Chiffon Cake with salted coconut cream served in an actual coconut. And like good sex, it was satisfying to the very end. I could say more, but the Yelp censors would delete my review.

Moving on to libations, the most unique thing you'll ever pass through your tongue is the salty-sweet Fish Sauce, complete with napa cabbage--yes napa cabbage--broth. Get it, drink it, thank me later. Or if you don't want ethanol, the Homemade Bael Juice is sweet and refreshing.

On personality, Bangkok Supper Club is as awesome as Fish Cheeks, but I think my wallet likes older sis more. Still, if someone else scores resies here again, I wouldn't say no.....

Our reservation was at 7:30 we got seated at 8. Hostess apologized as we waited and offered to start our cocktails at the host stand after waiting 20 minutes for our table. By the time we decided on what cocktail we wanted they sat us down. The hostess delivered our cocktails but no apology for the severe table delay. After waiting 30 minutes four our table, our waiter only offered us bottled water in hopes we would pay and when asked for tap he seemed annoyed. Appetizers came out quick but our entrees came around 8:50 when our reservation started at 7:30 and all dishes were brought at different times. They apologized but nothing else was really done. When we were ready for dessert our waiter took a while to grab our dirty entree dishes and to ask us what we wanted for dessert. Upon our dessert arriving, mid bite our check was placed on our table despite us asking for it and we felt rushed out.  Dishes were good but nothing special. We ordered the truffle tart (skip),  ceviche, bangkok hai yang, and curry sea bass. Ceviche and pandan dessert were some of the better dishes.

That Pork Jowl Garlic Fried Rice is going to get me coming back. Also loved the beef cheek Massaman. I am not the biggest fan of the sea bass but the sauce was really delicate. The service has been attentive the twice I have been there and the lightings are perfect for photos. May I say it is better than Fish Cheek?

Excellent drinks and atmosphere. The food was pretty good, but did feel it was pricey for the portion size. I like Fish Cheeks better, but this place definitely feels more elevated and nice for a special occasion or group dinner.

Words cannot describe how much I enjoyed dining here, definitely one of my top spots in New York!

I was lucky enough to snag a reservation for weekday dinner after stocking their page for weeks. We arrived early for our reservation, but the hostess was kind enough to seat us after a little wait.

Inside the ambiance was lively. The decor was simple retro. The space felt bustling. The service was extremely good as well. The staff took the time to answer of questions and give recommendations, making us feel very comfortable and in good hands. Now onto the best part, food and drinks!

The drink menu has some truly unique drinks, highly recommend you to try them!

Truffled pandan - for the experimental, it smells rich, like an olive oil, yet tastes like tropical drink, a creative combo!
Guava nam jim - this is the perfect drink for those who like lighter fruity drinks, it comes with some spicy roe which added a nice contrast to the sweet sips

With the food, it seems that you can't go wrong no matter what you order.

But you can't miss the pork jowl which seems to be one of their signature dishes. The pork with the crispy skin on top of the rice had magnificent flavor. The chilean sea bass curry was also rich and creamy and had a bit of a kick. We also had the octopus, the meat tasted great and it was a little spicy. Unfortunately they weren't serving dessert, so will have to come back to try that some time.

Overall, had an amazing time and higly recommend if you're able to snag a reservation!

Excellent meal at Bangkok Supper club with a couple of minor caveats. Loved the ceviche (spicier than expected but the cooling watermelon component was the perfect foil) and the beef tartare (delicious with ample kaffir lime leaf and a great pile of rice crackers) and the fried duck egg salad (my son in particular thought that was incredible - from the mouths of teens). The octopus is like every octopus dish in the city: ridiculously, annoyingly small with half a tentacle cut up in 3 pieces. Skip it - it was irritatingly tiny.

The chicken is INCREDIBLE. Holy hell, how do they make it so tender and juicy?  They should bottle the Nam Jim Jaew sauce. I would put that on everything. The sticky rice was kind of awful - chewy bordering on a hockey puck, nearly inedible (I love sticky rice - this misses the mark). 

The branzino was fine but just that. The pork jowl was excellent and the garlic rice it came with was incredible.

So, we wanted to love the drinks but I have to say: we didn't. The guava drink and the peach were probably the best we tried. We ordered the longan drink for our underage daughter at the recommendation of the waitress. It wasn't good - none of us at the table enjoyed it. We asked if we could order the mango for her instead. The waitress offered to take it off the bill but we ordered it so we said it was fine to leave it. When she brought the mango drink, my daughter took one sip and handed it to her brother (he had ordered the mango the first round) and asked him to taste it to see if it was the same as his. He said it tasted different. We tasted it.  It had MEZCAL in it. My kids are, well, clearly kids. We saw the waitress bring the drink to the bartender who confirmed she had taken the wrong one and indeed served our kids the boozy cocktail. Oops.

I have to say, the waitress wasn't particularly apologetic. We were cool about it as it was a mistake, but honestly? They should have taken THAT drink off our bill (they didn't).

There were a couple of other service missteps that have forced my hand to bring it down a star. Overall, it's a sleek, sexy place with really comfy seats, a great sound system that makes each table feel intimate and not too loud, some truly excellent food (and some kind of small stingy dishes -  looking at you, octopus), some interesting but not universally great drinks and finally, some hit or miss service. It's not a cheap meal. For 4 of us, it was nearly $450 with tip. I expect a pretty impeccable meal at that price, so here's hoping they keep getting towards the truly elevated experience for which they are clearly working.
Incredible and eclectic. New Thai restaurant, new style for NYC (and frankly much needed). Loved every moment here. Will be back many times.

A solid meal all around. 
The crudo with watermelon granita is bright, refreshing and spicy. An unexpected delight. 
The grilled chicken was moist and grilled to perfection. The pork jowl dish had flavor and crunch, and paired well with the rice it was served with. 
The pandan dessert was great. 
Def worth checking out. 
Service is efficient and friendly.

We dined here last night for the new years dinner and had an incredible time. I'm not sure why infatuation only gave this place a 7. 

This is one of the best meals I've had in the city in recent memory and the food and ambiance brought back fond memories of dinners I had during a recent trip in Asia.

The food here was just okay. Not a place that I would come
back to for dinner. The drinks were good with very original flavors. If I came back I would come for pre dinner drinks.

Not sure what all the hype is about. The food was mediocre at best. When factoring in the portion/price, I can confidently say any other Thai restaurant in NYC is better than this. Really don't understand what standards ppl are using to give this place such rave reviews.

Fish Cheeks is amazing so was really looking forward to trying Supper Club. Well what a major disappointment! Place is beautiful, drinks well concocted but the food left a lot to be desired. Octopus was really nice, prawns tasty and duck egg yummy. Should have stopped there. The whole branzino was WAY overcooked, and the "beef cheek" masaman was delivered as "short rib". What??? The runner said he's been trying to get them to change the "paper" menu for weeks. a six bite portion of short rib curry for $38??!! Unforgivable!! At $175/person, we'll stick to the East village option.

Really happy I was able to come and try the food. I thought the food was delicious albeit pricey. 

Service was great, staff were attentive and food came at a fairly good turnaround time. The decor of the restaurant was definitely modern, nothing that gave me Thai but it was a very pretty restaurant nonetheless. It was already buzzing at 5pm when the restaurant opened. My group and I tried several dishes:

- Yum Khai Dao - I enjoyed it. It's like a salad so It was more on the lighter side. Very good texture with the crunchy bits and had some acid and heat.

- Prawn Satay - Delicious. The sauce went really well with the prawn and honestly, you can't go wrong with grilled prawns! This dish is good for those that can't handle spice as well.

- Hokkaido Scallop Cerviche - I think this comes highly recommended but although it wasn't bad, it was just not my favorite among the dishes with big bold flavors. I do agree with the server that this is more of a light refreshing dish. The scallop was also sweet and you can definitely taste the freshness. 

Lin Yang - also very nice. Although not a top favorite, I think it's still a good choice especially for those seeking dishes with less heat. 

Pork Jowl - I think my favorite part of this dish is the rice. It's super flavorful! Would recommend to get.

Beef Cheek Massaman - My favorite dish of the night! Beef cheek was tender and the curry had so much flavor! 

Bangkok Gai Yang - Chicken was grilled to perfection. My only gripe is the sticky rice which they grilled. They over grilled our rice so it wasn't pleasant to eat since it was so hard lol

I would come back if someone chooses this spot but not in a rush to be back.

Hottest place in town charged me $200 when I canceled less than 24 hours in advance.. although I made the reservation less than 24 hours in advance! Two in my party were sick and I'm sorry I couldn't honor the reservation ( Resy will tell you I always do!)!but I was not a no show and I'm pretty sure that table got filled up in a NY second once I cancelled the reservation. 
Totally disappointed in this greedy ethic. I also think, and I took a photo of it and I'm posting .. that at the point of cancellation you should advise your patron that it WILL trigger a $50 per person fee. Saying that it "may trigger a fee " is misleading.

Really loved the placed.  Atmosphere was fun, server was pleasant & attentive, but their food really stood out.  Every dish had strong, distinct wonderful flavoring and often on the spicy side. For apps we had the steak tartare,the shrimp and the grilled octopus.  All good but the octopus was our favorite.  For mains, theSea Bass in curry sauce and Massaman Beef cheeks were both outstanding and the grilled bok choy vegetable was amazingly good. Can't wait to go back and highly recommend the restaurant.  One of the best we have had.

I LOVE Fish Cheeks so I was really eager to try this spot. The ambience is definitely warm & inviting, everything is family style. We had the oyster mushroom salad, fish curry,& eggplant. Everything was great! The fish curry reminded me of Fish Cheek's crab curry, oyster mushrooms were hearty & delicious. The eggplant was good & unique but I probably wouldn't order again. Service was also great, she was super attentive & gave great recommendations.

My friends and I arrived for a 7:30 reservation on a Wednesday evening. The menu was great and I could've easily ordered any dish. We started with cocktails and then ordered the mushroom salad and prawn satay. Both were delicious but they brought out only two shrimp when we asked to pay extra for three. They took the entire dish back and remade it which delayed the course. Not a big deal but was a little off. For the mains we tried the ba jang lobster, Chilean sea bass chakram curry and Bangkok chicken. The chicken was awesome! I would recommend. No bad dishes though! I would go back if someone else was treating.
Go with a group and just get the whole menu. The team has outdone themselves! So good we got the duck eggs twice

I was so happy to see this new Thai place open up in west village. It's always busy and popular every time I walk by, and I was finally able to get a reservation. 

First off, the cocktails were incredible. While more on the expensive side, each drink I sampled was unique and delicious in its own right. I would recommend the truffled pandan, beets n cream, and raw rice. 

Next, the food. I was impressed with literally every dish I had, which is rare! My favorite was the beef cheeks massaman curry, but the yum khai dao and pork jowl were yummy as well. Our server recommended we order at 5-6 dishes for 3 people citing small portions. But I was glad we only got those three because we were full after! 

I am already looking forward to coming back as soon as I can snag another reservation.

Bangkok Supper Club is the new(ish) restaurant from Fish Cheeks. Bangkok Supper Club is truly a step up on all levels. The food, the cocktails, the service and the restaurant interior are all amazing. We didn't try a single dish that wasn't superb. So many more dishes that we need to try!

Thursday 7:30pm 

Ambiance :sleek , clean , open , airy 

Food:  elevated Thai , imagine traditional flavors presented in a more sophisticated way .  We had shrimp , fish , green beans , pork jowl and the only dessert available ( I hope they add more in the near future ).

Service : from the hostess to servers , they were friendly and attentive .  I dig the unique outfit .

It was one of the hottest restaurants in the city right now so the reservations were fully booked a month ahead. The resy opened at midnight. I had high hopes since I loved their sister restaurant Fish cheeks. The price here was def on the pricier side but everything was so delicious.

- Hokkaido scallop ceviche: the scallop was ok, but the sauce and the watermelon all together made it a pretty refreshing and solid dish.
- Lin Yang: beef tongue was so tender and flavorful. My favorite!
- Pork jowl: the pork cheeks was well-seasoned, tender and had the perfect fat proportion. It was their most popular dish for a good reason. Another of my favorite.
- Sea bass curry: this was another solid dish, not as special as lin yang and pork jowl, but really tasty (and also pretty spicy)
- Dessert: they only had one that day. I'm not sure whether it changed everyday but mine was sweet potato ice cream on some sticky rice with some dried coconut. You should totally get this dessert. It has many flavor and it was so yummy.

Overall, i love this place and I would totally come back once the resy situation gets better.

This place has been popping up all over my Tiktok therefore I knew that I needed to try this place. My bestie managed to snag a 5 pm reservation (that is when they opened) unfortunately we were running extremely late (we did call to let them know) but they still honored our reservation even though we got there at 6 pm (we were warned that we had to leave by 7 pm since that was when the next reservation was so I think that the reservations are for two hours. The vibes in the place was very interesting, dim lighting but still very fun. It honestly smelled soo good though. 

We quickly glanced at the menu and placed our orders: 
For appetizers we got the scallop ceviche - honestly, I was not a fan of the dish. It was much more spicier than I thought it would be which I think took away from the scallop flavors for me. I would pass on this dish in the future. 
For pain means we got the pork jowl which is their most famous and popular dish and for good reason - this dish is a must. The flavors were amazing, the pork was so tender and not rough at all, mild spicy after taste. So good - highly recommend. We also got the lobster sticky rice - this is great if you are a fan of sticky rice because the rice was super sticky (LOL) but great flavors def recommend. 

For drinks - I got the peach moonshine which was way too strong for me but I think it would be good for other people.

Overall great vibes and I would come back just for the pork jowl and their desserts looked really good!

4 star for food, 2.5 for drinks. 

I've been trying to avoid coming to brand new places as usually there are operational issues to be worked out for new places. I broke this rule for this one because it seemed pretty hyped up and I love fish cheeks. Unfortunately it reaffirmed my theory that new places need time to work out kinks. 

We ordered several cocktails, and one nonalcoholic drink for a pregnant friend. We ordered prawns and beef tongue for appetizers, beef cheeks, lobster, sea bass, and NY strip steak for main. Issue number one, app came out before our drinks. Not major but a bit weird. Issue number two, when our drinks came, the nonalcoholic drink reeked mezcal. We asked our waiter, she's like oh it's nonalcoholic. We all tasted it, and it 100% had mezcal in it. So we asked the waiter to take it back, who looked confused at the time. Then I saw her tried it at the counter and realized it indeed had alcohol in it. Maybe it's okay to mess up drinks from time to time. But isn't it similar to messing up food allergy - it's dangerous. 

Foos was good, nothing amazing except the beef cheeks, which had great flavors and very tender texture. Everything else was good, although nothing to rave about. 

Would I come back here anytime soon? No. I'd rather go to fish cheeks.

The Bangkok Supper Club truly felt like a home away from home. Chef Max's classic pork jowl garlic fried rice, a dish reminiscent of his dad's school-day cooking, transports you to that nostalgic time with every savory bite--a mouthful of cherished memories. Their innovative prawn satay, featuring cashew sauce instead of the traditional peanut, adds a delightful twist, making each bite a luxurious experience. And the Chilean sea bass chakram curry delivers the perfect kick, turning every bite into a new culinary adventure. A big thank you to Chat and the team for being fantastic hosts. Excited to share this experience with more friends and family!

This meal at @bangkoksupperclubnyc is one of the most memorable ones this year! I'm so lucky to get to try this new addition of creative Thai cuisine in the city - did not disappoint!

I was impressed and enjoyed every dish, and I think my favorite was the scallop ceviche...was not expecting that spice to kick in like that! The pork jowl is their most popular dish and it was very beautiful and delicious, but I equally enjoyed the chicken and grilled rice.

The interior design and great service were such a bonus since I feel like many famous NYC restaurants have been lacking those recently. 100% recommend to visit...if you can snatch a reservation!

This place is a 10/10. Everything that I tried on their menu was absolutely delicious and their cocktails were all masterfully curated. We sat at the bar and all the bartenders + servers were really friendly. The bartender took our order and gave some great recommendations for both cocktails and food. My boyfriend and I got their Truffled Pandan and Guava Nam Jin. Both drinks were exquisite and presented many different flavors with every sip. As for the food, we got the Lin yang (beef tongue), pork jowl, and Chilean sea bass curry. Amazing would be an understatement for all three dishes that we tried. If I had to choose one dish that is a must, it would be the Lin Yang beef tongue. Expect a flavor blast, it is so, so good. I only wish I had a bigger stomach so I could order more. Unfortunately, we didn't have room for dessert but it looked really good and the person sitting next to us devoured his, so I'd assume it's worth a try if you still have room after the delicious savory meal. Highly recommend!

We went here with a group of 4 on a Wednesday! We had made a reservation a month prior! Aesthetics and service were superb. Overall I enjoyed the food, but also the cocktails were highlights for me. Portions of food are small and are meant to be shared. For the value to portion size ratio, I feel its more on the expensive side. Quality and execution were good, but it can tend to come off a bit salty in some dishes.

What we ordered :
Scallops ceviche
Fried Duck egg salad
Beef tartare

Beef cheeks massaman curry
Lobster over sticky rice
Pork jowl

I personally liked the fried duck egg salad and the beef tartare. The lobster and sticky rice my personal favorite in the main entreés. The cocktails here are a must! They are adventurous and experimental, yet it works well!

Would I come back? I think I would but for special occasions.
