I was really hoping to like this place, as it is a new addition to the neighborhood and we don't have a lot of Thai places.

However, our server was really not friendly which dampened the vibe. 

As for food/drinks we were very underwhelmed which lead us to cash out right before even ordering entrees. The hostess recommended a cocktail but it honestly tasted like straight gin and had a Giant ice cube in it. If you took out the ice cube there would be no drink. 

We tried the ceviche, which was not ceviche at all. It had these frozen watermelon cubes on top which was just a complete miss on the dish. It kind of tasted like pop rocks on top of fish. When our server came back she said "Oh is it too spicy?", the dish had ZERO spice and she basically profiled us that we couldn't handle it.

We tried the octopus as well which tasted good but very small portion. When a staff member placed this on the table, I remarked that the portion was small and he agreed with me and didn't have any positive comments. 

Overall, I'm not sure management knows that the service is just unprofessional. When paying a high dollar you expect to be treated with respect. Sadly just another west village place where they make sure you have plenty of overpriced cocktails but not enough to eat. I won't be returning to Bangkok Sucker Club.

New kid in town, and it's Thai so definitely had to check it out. I came on a Saturday for walk in, around 630pm the wait was around an hour but i heard it was hard to book resy here. I liked everything that was ordered, some more than others, but overall very satisfied with the quality of the food here. Must get dishes are the park Jowl and the duck fried egg as well as the beef tongue! 

-the pork jowl is their specialty-the garlic baked rice with pork rinds was straight up crack , and I told myself I was not gonna eat carbs ....this says how good this is 
-the drink I got specifically was very unique with intricate flavors (the one I got was the gin fat washed truffle oil, apple juice infused with coffee and thyme herbs, pandan syrup and malic acid 
-fried duck egg was very refreshing. I've never had a dish like this before 
-beef tongue was so tender and flavorful!

Great modern Thai food from the team that brought us Fish Cheeks. Bangkok Supper Club makes modern renditions of Thai late night snacks. The restaurant features an open kitchen with moody lighting. Service was pretty quick but we weren't rushed at all. Our server did a great job breaking down the menu and explaining the various dishes.

For the table, we ordered the yum khai dao, sea bass curry, Hokkaido scallop ceviche, and pork jowl. Dishes are served family-style and are meant to be shared, however, you could easily order a dish for yourself if you want (the portions aren't huge). The flavors evoke a balance of classic Thai flavors: salty, sweet, sour and spicy. Everything was good, but the pork jowl was phenomenal, a must-order dish. The Hokkaido scallop ceviche surprised us with the addition of watermelon granita and was probably one of the more interesting dishes I've had this year. 

If I were to nitpick a bit, I think the cocktails we had was a little more miss than hit. I felt the drinks I had fell a bit flat.

Overall, Bangkok Supper Club is a fun addition to the West Village. Come here with a group and share a bunch of dishes. Chances are you'll find something to talk about.

Solid 4 stars! -1 star just for the price for portion size, but a great place for a more upscale visit if you have an occasion (or just manage to get a good reservation time!) 

All the cocktails our group tried were great. Both apps - the octopus and egg dish were uniquely prepared. Pork jowl rice was the highlight for me, eggplant was good as well. Steak was cooked perfectly with a unique spicy sauce. Lobster was well-cooked but nothing special, wasn't well incorporated into the crispy sticky rice which would've been good on its own. Beans and peas were decent for balancing out the meal with some veggies.
Great food great service can't wait to go back, modern Thai dishes was something I can't forget

Definitely get the curry! This is a more upscale feel than fish cheeks so since I'm the type of person to value the food more than the ambiance, I prefer fish cheeks also for the price.

Service was fantastic and space was nice. It's hard to get a reservation right now but bar seating is first come first serve!
Everything was amazing. Beef cheeks curry was my favorite thing. The beets n cream was also good. Service was great. I have nothing more to say except I will be thinking about this meal for a while

Snagged a last minute resy at this trendy new restaurant and it did not disappoint! It's definitely on the pricey side but some of the dishes like the scallops & pork jowl were to worth it. They were both a 10/10 with the perfect balance of flavors. 

We also got the prawns which were nice and juicy but tasted like a lot of prawn dishes I've had before- enjoyable but not mind blowing. The lobster was also good but could benefit with a citrusy drizzle to bring it alive! 

- @nyconthetsble

Hands down the best new restaurant in NYC!
Food, service, ambiance A+!         
Must try for Thai food lovers

- superior service
- our wait staff was extremely kind and efficient - constantly filling water and replacing dishes while cleaning the table
- appetizers and cocktails came very quickly - very good quality food
- favorite appetizer is octopus - better than most top Michelin restaurants 
- best entree is the pork rice - the spice level was perfect
- food came very quickly which was excellent - total dinner time 70 minutes 
- atmosphere feels upscale with fun salsa dancing music

Excellent Thai food here that tastes authentic and great pace. Very impressed.

Food is slightly a miss but service and atmosphere are there.

Beef Cheeks Curry was soft, tender and delicious. $37, but didn't feel like I got the value out of the price

Pork Jowl, while the pork was tender and a lime was provided, the food was incredibly salty. While aesthetically pleasing, it was hard to finish given the saltiness.

Scallop Ceviche, refreshing but spicy. The watermelon shaved ice over it is a first, but works well to help cut the spice down

Mushroom Garden Salad, a little spicy, $18, simply some veggies and oyster mushrooms, while it was an enjoyable salad, the price was a little high.

Overall the price for the food doesn't make this place a restaurant I would return to, the ambience and service is nice, but this is NYC, we have plenty of restaurants that have nice service and ambience, food is what makes you survive.

We started off with the ceviche and Bronzino which were light and great way to start off before the heavier larger dishes. Was also informed that the restaurant still does not have their gas line hooked up so all dishes have been done over electric/induction. Pretty impressive considering the grilled/charred flavors from the veggie and fish. A bit disappointed by the jowl rice and curry. Pork jowl was overly dry and curry was not memorable (I'm sure everyone in nyc has their own go to Thai spot  with better massaman) The highlight was the drink menu (raw rice fish sauce) and infuses many southeast Asian flavors. 5/5 for the drinks, large plates a bit of a let down 3.5/5

Bangkok Supper Club is potentially the best upscale Thai restaurant I've had in NY so far. Ambience, food flavor, cocktails -- all were fantastic!

DRINKS:
They have an amazing selection of custom cocktails across the board. The strawberry toast cocktail was pretty accurate in flavor, but definitely spirit forward. However, the fish sauce cocktail and smokey milk stole the show. Super balanced flavors and remain so throughout the rest of the meal.

FOOD:
I would not recommend the beef tartare. The flavor is overly salty and the texture isn't super soft. While I appreciate the paper thin shrimp chip rendition, it doesn't add much to the dish.

Everything else was delicious. 
- Hokkaido scallop ceviche was refreshing and light. Just a warning, it does have a spicy kick to it. 
- The beef tongue was so tender, I wish there was more of this. 
- Pork jowl was so well flavored that we bought a massive bag at H-mart afterwards to make at home. 
- The lobster was obviously high quality, but I also really liked the crispy sticky rice base that comes with it.
- The coconut ice cream dessert was also SO GOOD. Just the right amount of sweetness and thickness texture, paired with the chewiness of the cornbread. 

Needless to say I look forward to coming back and trying everything else.

so many new thai spots in the city it's quite the trend in nyc. the good news is my thai friend says it was definitely authentic (except the branzino), the bad news is that it's essentially dressed up casual thai street food but at like 5000x the price in BKK. good spice levels on the dishes, no dilution there. food was delicious but dont' expect to see too many thai people in there later on, would be like new yorkers paying $20 a slice of joe's in thailand. I'd go back, if someone was paying for me.

Food: 8/10
Value: 3/10
Service: 9/10
Vibe: 8/10

My wife and I walked in and were able to get a seat at the bar within ten minutes on a Thursday night (have patience people). Michelle, the hostess was lovely and told us a little about the menu along with what to expect for the night.

Once seated, Ali the awesome bartender recommended some lovely drinks that my wife and I had throughout our journey at this establishment. We were asked to move over early in our dining experience a few spots down which my wife and I didn't mind and we thought we ended up at a better location. The energy in the whole place was electric. It felt like old NYC days. The people next to us were lovely and we chatted them up and talked about what looked great on the menu.

The food was phenomenal! It seemed like every dish had lovely heat with added textures for a nice balance. Pro Tip-make sure you get the pork jowl and mix that with the curry...thanks Paul!

We briefly spoke with one of the owners Chat who was a super nice guy and thanked him for the lovely evening my wife and I had!

What an awesome addition to the neighborhood. We will definitely be back!

We didn't have a reservation and waited a sad 3 hours for this place. We were super upset with how the servers handled this situation, constantly giving us false hope and reassuring us that we'd be seated "soon". At one point, the server said "sorry I'm not sure what's going on right now, they're trying something new" (in regards to the seating action plan). This was super frustrating because even if you knew that as a server and it was true, why would you ever say that to a customer?? Do not come without a reservation, the walk-in wait time is pure agony and they just clearly don't accommodate to walk-in's like a normal restaurant would (i.e. reserve x amount of seats per night for walk-ins).

We finally were able to get seated after we complained to the manager. He (Paul) could clearly tell we were very unhappy customers and did his best to make the situation better by giving us free things on the house (appetizer, drinks, dessert). This, and how the food itself was amazing, is the reason that this rating is 3 stars instead of 1. I would come again for the food, and I really hope that by then, the staff are trained better so that no one would ever have to experience that type of service ever again.

Amazing experienced and delicious Thai food. The decor was great inside, loved the open kitchen concept. Pat our server was so sweet recommended an excellent dish and explained the restaurant inspiration story. 

My favorite dishes were Ceviche and Chakram curry, flavorful with a good kick of spiciness.I enjoyed every single bite of its.
Dessert was the best part!! The salted caramel coconut ice cream just made the perfect ending. 

This place was worth the hype!!!
Will definitely come back.

Let me start of by saying the service was wonderful . Our server was pat and she was very kind, personable , and helpful . She was well versed in the dishes and her recommendations were on point . 

As for the food while it was good, I do prefer fish cheeks . While the dishes here are more elevated and sleek with smaller portions, I do prefer the Laid back family style portions of fish cheeks as well as the flavor profile of fish cheeks. 

We ordered the beef tartare ( was ok) , the mushroom salad ( didn't care for it ), the scallop ceviche (was very good ), the pork belly with garlic rice (was ok), the lobster ( small portion and the memorable part was the sticky rice ), the sea bass curry (which was our favorite dish of the night ) . I would recommend the scallop ceviche , the sea bass curry , and based on reviews the beef cheek curry which we were going to order. They only have one desert which was very tasty and not too sweet .

We managed to try everything on the menu. The best small dish was the Yum Kai Dai -- the three different presentations of duck egg created such interesting texture and flavors. The Lin Yang (beef tongue) was soft with well-balanced flavors. 

Of the large dishes, we really enjoyed the Pork Jowl. The pork was soft and the rice had great balance of acid and crunch. The Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry was creamy, just a little spicy and topped with a nice buttery juicy piece of fish. 

The happiest ending was the signature dessert, the sticky rice cake with caramelized palm sugar ice cream topped with toasted coconut. The ice cream was smooth and had just the right amount of sweetness. 

Of the drinks, the standout was the truffle pandan. The smell of the truffle made it seem like it would be a strong drink, but it went down very smoothly, finish with a nice pandan flavor. 

The atmosphere was intimate and laid back. We also loved the open kitchen concept. Watching Max delicately place herbs onto the dishes made the experience even more personal.

Upon entering Bangkok Supper Club, I was immediately struck by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant's tasteful decor, featuring traditional Thai elements, created a cozy and intimate setting.

server very nice she came to introduce about inspiration of the restaurant from Bangkok lat night scene food with open kitchen concept. Being able to see the chefs at It was fascinating to watch the meticulous preparation and attention to detail that went into each dish.

Drink  Truffled Pandan 
strong truffled oil but after i sip the drink very refreshing with vanilla aroma from pandan leaf.

Speaking of dishes,  i ordered 
Yum kai down which come with fried duck egg trout roe and chicken cured York eggs.

Mushroom salad Charcoal grill lettuce with coconut dressing sauce.

Pork jowl. !!!! i died for it. 
i love the pork cheeks and fat part of pork crispy texture from fried shallots.

Bangkok Gai Yang  grilled tender chicken served with sticky rice patty and nam jim jeaw sauce 

The prices at Bangkok Supper Club were reasonable considering the quality of the ingredients and the impeccable service. The value for money was undeniable, making it an ideal destination for both special occasions and casual dining.

One of my husband's many talents is walking into a restaurant and scoring that impossible to reserve table.  So we found ourselves seated at the bar at 8:30 p.m. on a Saturday night, toasting our good fortune.  Service is warm and impeccable here - everyone seems truly concerned about you having a good time.  The bar is elegant, the dining room swanky, with prices to match.  

However, as a celebration of Bangkok's late night food scene, this "upgrade" in sophistication and price seemed mismatched.  The menu lends itself to snacking and drinking - I found it difficult to create a whole meal here because all of the dishes seem protein heavy.  I found myself craving something vegetable based, but there was really nothing on offer.  Also, whoever heard of a $36 snack?  Or a $16 beer?  Everything we ate was delicious, but small plates are called "small" for a reason.  We arrived starving.  We went to work on the octopus and shrimp small plates.  We had ordered the pork to share, and we quickly added the chicken mid-meal because we were afraid we would leave hungry.  Actually, main courses are generously portioned.  So, I would advise ordering one small plate and two entrees.  That being said, we probably won't be back any time soon.  Sixteen dollars for a beer is ludicrous, and Thai Diner does this scene better.

I have been here twice time since they opened . I love the atmosphere  ,the kitchen is open- concept in the back,
Our server " Pat"   she was very nice and professional recommended the food and introduced the story and concept  inspiration of the restaurant.

I ordered the drink Beet and cream it perfectly flavor drink for  the people don't like strong drink.
Food  I love Goi  and the pork jowl  2dish must to be try!!!!
For dessert  very limited (sold out when I ordered) but I will definitely come back to try.
Awesome authentic Thai food that's super flavorful, service was friendly and ambiance was very modern. Definitely worth trying their cocktails also - not too sweet and had such unique flavors!

Delicious and authentic Thai food. Managed to snag a resy at a decent time albeit it was a Monday night. Nice list of cocktails with Asian flavors. Tried a few and enjoyed it. 

We shared our starter and mains - mushroom salad and grilled chicken. Both were very good with a nice kick of spiciness.

Wil definitely come back and try other dishes!

Couldn't get a resie but walked in just fine! Love fish cheeks so had to try this spot out. The scallop ceviche was a bit spicy  but very good. The beef tartare was decent but could've used more flavor. Lobster over rice was very good - hard to go wrong with lobster. The coconut and mochi cake dessert was quite good. Very lively spot. Service was fairly good too. Enjoyed the bael drink.

I was more disappointed with the atmosphere and service than I was with the food. The food was a solid three stars, but the atmosphere & service was one star at best. Why? When I ordered the prawns the server said OH THAT'S SPICY basically insinuating I wouldn't like it and that I should order something else. When I ordered the octopus the server said UMM THAT ONE IS REALLY FISHY basically insinuating I wouldn't like it and that I should order something else. Neither my dining companion nor myself are Thai, but rather than "guilty until proven innocent," they could have asked us if we were familiar with Thai cuisine (YES, WE BOTH ARE!!!), but instead it created a continued cloud of separation, as if the food was too good for us or we weren't good enough for the food? Mind you, the server wasn't Thai, either, this tone must have been instructed by management. Because only management can authorize free samples being REQUIRED before taking an order for a cocktail. The server would not accept my order for the Fish Sauce cocktail without me first having a sample, which of course took a few minutes to arrive for the sample, and then took an additional few minutes to arrive once I approved of the cocktail. Actually, the cocktail was underwhelming, and I have no idea how anybody could be offended by it or why anyone would send it back, but perhaps because the servers are doing such a poor job at advocating and encouraging, there is an overall tone established which is the opposite of Thai-inviting... 

As we attempted to order second courses, the server kept not just repeating what we were saying but "correcting it," for the sake of clarity and precision I always order things as they're listed on the menu, so when I ordered the Whole Branzino, I was interrupted with "The Fish, okay, what else?" but since there were multiple fish items on the menu I repeated that I wanted the Whole Branzino and of course the server retorted even louder "OKAY, SO, THE FISH, WHAT ELSE?" When ordering an additional second course, sadly and unfortunately, the same exact thing happened all over again. "Crying Tiger, please." "OKAY SO THE FISH AND THE BEEF,* but since there are multiple beef items on the menu, I wanted to ensure that it was indeed the Crying Tiger, and got admonished with "THE BEEF." It seems their preferred shorthand system takes precedent over actual interactions and communications with guests. Because when I ordered my second cocktail, although repeated a few times, it came out wrong. 

Anyway, the food. Prawns were well-done, I would have preferred medium to medium-rare to retain some moisture; they even took the head off and removed the innards presumably to not offend anyone. There was no beautiful Thai grill flavor that I love so much. Same with the Octopus, it seemed they pulled off most of the purple skin so that sadly there could not be any deep-char or crunch or chew. Crying Tiger was fine but had a lot of inedible gristle. Whole Branzino was the best thing all night, beautifully juicy, wonderfully flaky skin, but very bland overall. It seems that everything was muted and tone-down for the audience. Even though the Chef and Owner are Thai, the food seems like it's American with condiments influenced by Thailand, which is NOT what I wanted.

***2.5 STARS*** Overall a bad experience and probs would've given it a 1 star but the food ended up being pretty good and the manager did make an effort to amend the issues. 

We arrived before they opened so around 4:55pm and there was already a long line. Unfortunately our party of 3 didn't get in the first round of walk ins, we were told probably 1 hour wait so we were like ok that's fine. About 1 hr 15 min later we came back and asked what place we were in line and they said 8th. However, there were a lot of parties leaving at the time plus we felt like we were in too deep already so we decided to just stick it out for a little longer. Then at the 1.5 hr mark, i asked them again and was told there was only 1 party named "Kevin" ahead of us.

However, we kept waiting and waiting, seeing people come and go. We even witnessed them seat two parties who weren't even on the waitlist but said "I'm friends with [presumed staff member]" right in front of us.... We ask the host again what's going on and he shrugs and said "sorry I don't know what's happening with the tables, I think they're doing something new, I'm not in charge" which was completely unprofessional like why would you say that? Just don't say anything at all if you're not clear about what's going on, OR at the very least offer to ask someone who does know what's going on. He and the other guy at the host just kept ignoring us otherwise and making awkward eye contact for an hour but saying nothing. It's 2 hours 45 min wait at this point btw - AND to make matters even more confusing, 1) we have seen several tables completely vacant for over an hour while we're waiting and 2) we overhear from their convo that "Kevin" (the one party ahead of us since the 1.5 hr mark) hasn't even arrived yet even though tons of other parties have come and go... so are they reserving a table for him indefinitely or what? 

Eventually we flag down the manager Paul and finally something actually happens. He'a super apologetic and moves things around to create 3 spots at the bar. What pissed me off wasn't that there was a long wait for walk in bc I get that it's very unpredictable, but how unprofessional and unhelpful the two employees at the host table were despite KNOWING that we had been waiting for an entire 2 hr 45 min after arriving before the restaurant even opened. Yeah we should've flagged down the manager much earlier instead of relying on them two, and probably should've gone more Karen to be taken seriously, but wtf?

Anyway, we ordered a couple dishes which were delicious and Paul also added on another appetizer, dessert, and drinks on the house as an apology for the "miscommunication and system issues" that led to this fiasco. I acknowledge that the food was pretty fire - our favs were the Goi and yum khai dao - and now that they did make an effort to rectify the situation, I'd maybe consider coming back to eat ONLY if I had a reservation (but they're supposedly booked out for months).

This was FUN! We waited before opening to grab bar seats and had a really great time.

Bartender/host Chris was extremely thoughtful and conversational! 

Loved, loved the Pork Jowl! The pork pieces were so moist and on top a bed of crispy garlic rice that reminded me to some Filipino garlic rice dishes. Also fair warning across the board for those sensitive to spicy - although all dishes weren't jarringly spicy, it was enough to ask for milk throughout the courses.

The other stand out was the dessert! Sweet potato ice cream with coconut chips. Amazing!!! I'm not too big of an ice cream fan, but I loved loved this. It's so subtle and refreshing after all the savory items before.

Highly recommend coming back!

Absolutely delicious!! This is a new spot opened by the team behind Fish Cheeks and they did not disappoint. Aside from its amazingly chic decor, the lighting and seating gave intimate vibes - perfect for friends or a date night. 

The menu offered lots to try with perfect sharing portions that left you wanting more. My group and I practically tried the entire cocktail menu - all amazingly unique flavors you wouldn't find elsewhere (a drink with truffle aromatics and another drink with fish sauce?? Yes please!)

We tried 4 apps - fried duck eggs salad, beef tartare, octopus, prawn - and 3 mains - pork jowl, beef cheeks curry, sea bass curry. Everything was incredibly flavorful and tender. While not as spicy as its sister restaurant, still left us wanting more. One star docked for its menu - while I did enjoy everything we've ordered I do wish there were noodles or more sides

author.location: Downtown Jersey City, Jersey City, NJ

reviews.review: Nice atmosphere, attentive service, great food, and good cocktails. However, the charge for beer was outrageous - $16 for one Singha. Keep in mind each cocktail was around $18-23. At most other locations charging ~$20 per cocktail, beers are typically max $10-12. We loved the dishes we tried (fried egg, beef tongue, prawns, and pork jowl), but will remember this restaurant by the outrageous beer price. The fried egg appetizer was great - acidic and spicy. We also enjoyed the prawn satay with the peanut sauce, but the star was the pork jowls with the rice (not pictured). As far as cocktails, I did really enjoy the Guava Nam Jim and raspberry miso cocktails, but the price of beer really surprised us.

New spot that just opened two weeks ago from the folks behind Fish Cheeks. You have to get the scallop ceviche & steak tartare! Pork jowl was phenomenal but I think the spotlight has to be on the apps. They ran out of the popular duck appetizer tonight so would probably get that since it seems to be a big hit. Service is very nice & it was popping on a Monday 9pm. Must come!

One star off for service, but I get it's a new shop. Servers were nice but forgot to put in a dish which later sold out that night (the duck). They offered a free appetizer in a replacement and later told us that management said it could no longer be free after we ordered so offered free mocktails. When the bill came, we were billed for all items.

By some miracle we got in within a week of their opening. My only regret is not bringing more friends so we could try more dishes. 

Waiters are courteous, attentive, polite and friendly. Overall the food, ambiance and staff made the evening a delight!

We decided to try things we didn't necessarily read about, so we could provide a new opinion and are glad we did! 

For apps we tried the yum khai dao & hakkaido scallop ceviche. 
Lots of reviews are talking about the yum khai dao, but the ceviche was where my heart was at. I think The yum khai dao is for those with a specific taste palette...I would have preferred more of the sauce the egg was sitting in, and was hoping for the caviar to add an extra oomph. I loved how perfectly the egg was cooked, runny, but not flowing onto the plate. Probably too low brow for Bangkok supper club, but would have liked to dip the fried egg in the sauce it sat atop. 

As for the ceviche, it was divine. My only call out is to ensure your bite has a small amount of the watermelon granita, so the scallop won't instantly freeze in your mouth. But once the granita melts, I would definitely lap it up with your spoon as the combination with the mint and watermelon rind was delightful. 

For the mains we opted against there pork jowl & branzino, even though everyone is talking about them and we went for the Ba Jang lobster & beef cheeks massaman curry. All dishes here require you to taste everything in the dish in one bite, don't attempt to deconstruct & eat the lobster separate from the sticky rice, together it's delightful, but solo, they will come off as bland. However, in general we preferred the curry to the lobster. Our thought was that the lobster could have had a more robust flavor profile, so in comparison we loved the curry. 

The beef cheeks  broke apart easily and the curry was beautiful, and not too rich. I loved all the vegetables found in the dish. 

For two people, I was suspecting that 4 dishes would leave us very full, but it was the perfect amount of food leaving us satisfied and happy. 

The ambiance and decor is great inside, and it was very cool to experience a restaurant within their opening weeks. Would recommend people give it a go, and open their minds to the new dishes Bangkok Supper Club is offering.

A very nice new restaurant that is getting a lot of hype despite being just two weeks old. You will be very hard pressed to get a reservation because there are so many people wanting to get in.

The cocktails are outstanding, very nice selection of sweeter options reminiscent of what you might expect in Southern Asian countries.

Service was very good, food came out relatively fast and the table was reset for each round of courses.

My friends loved the meat courses with the pork jowl being a fan favorite.

If you are gluten free, vegan or vegetarian this is not the restaurant for you. There was a single vegetarian dish available (mushrooms) although after some discussion with chef, the manager was kind enough to debut the crispy fried tofu. By the time you read this two dishes will apparently be available and the manager promised a third for next time, so I'll have to see if I can get in again!

everything is perfect! My favorite drinks are guava nam jim and beets n cream.
My favorite dish is pork jowl
